title: 2026 AFD CSO Call for Expressions of Project Intentions: Funding Opportunity for Civil Society Organizations in Developing Countries
summary: The Agence Française de Développement (AFD) has opened the 2026 Call for Expressions of Project Intentions for Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) , providing an opportunity for eligible civil society organizations to submit projects for potential AFD co-financing in 2027. The call is designed to strengthen the contribution of civil society organizations to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) , international solidarity, local development and policy change. For the 2026 edition, AFD has introduced a single call covering both French CSOs and locally governed CSOs , with the objective of identifying projects led by civil society organizations in partner countries that could receive financing in 2027. The call is particularly relevant for eligible CSOs working on development, social transformation, international solidarity, climate vulnerability, civic engagement and other areas aligned with sustainable development priorities. Applications must be submitted through AFD s OSCar online platform , and organizations that do not already have an OSCar account must request account creation by September 15, 2026 . The final deadline for submitting project intentions is October 9, 2026, at 6:00 PM Paris time . Overview of the 2026 AFD CSO Call The 2026 CSO Call for Expressions of Project Intentions is part of AFD s CSO Initiatives mechanism, which supports projects led by civil society organizations. The mechanism recognizes the role of civil society in identifying development challenges and designing initiatives that respond to the needs of communities. Rather than limiting CSOs to projects defined by external institutions, AFD s framework recognizes the right of initiative , allowing eligible organizations to propose projects that they have developed themselves. For the 2026 call, AFD is seeking project intentions that can potentially be shortlisted for financing in 2027 . The initiative aims to achieve two closely connected objectives: Strengthen civil society organizations in France and AFD intervention countries. Generate concrete development impacts for beneficiary populations while contributing to local policy and sustainable development. What Is the AFD CSO Initiatives Mechanism? The CSO Initiatives (CSO-I) mechanism is an AFD financing mechanism for projects led by French and locally governed civil society organizations. It is designed to support the capacity and effectiveness of civil society actors while enabling them to implement initiatives that contribute to development and international solidarity. Through this mechanism, AFD can support CSOs that are working to address development challenges and create meaningful, measurable benefits for communities. The mechanism is therefore particularly relevant to organizations that already have the institutional capacity, project experience and development-oriented mission needed to implement a substantial initiative. Objectives of the 2026 Call The 2026 call operates within France s broader development and international solidarity framework. It falls under France s 2021 Framework and Programming Act on Development and International Solidarity , adopted on August 4, 2021. It also aligns with France s Strategy for Civil Society and Civic Engagement for 2023–2027 , the conclusions of the Presidential Council for International Partnerships from April 2025, and AFD Group s 2025–2030 Strategy . The call consequently forms part of a wider effort to strengthen civil society participation in sustainable development and international cooperation. Key objectives include: Supporting the role of civil society organizations in achieving the Sustainable Development Goals . Strengthening the institutional and operational capacity of CSOs. Supporting initiatives developed by civil society organizations themselves. Generating concrete benefits for communities and beneficiary populations. Contributing to local policy development. Supporting international solidarity and sustainable development. Increasing the participation of locally governed CSOs in development financing. Who Can Apply for the AFD CSO Call? The call is open to eligible civil society organizations , rather than individual applicants. Two broad categories of CSOs are relevant: 1. French Civil Society Organizations French CSOs are eligible under the CSO Initiatives mechanism and can submit project intentions in accordance with the requirements of the call. 2. Locally Governed Civil Society Organizations Locally governed CSOs in countries eligible for Official Development Assistance (ODA) can also be eligible for direct AFD financing under specific conditions. This represents an important feature of the 2026 call because locally governed organizations are not automatically excluded from AFD financing simply because they are based outside France. Eligibility Requirements for Locally Governed CSOs According to the call, locally governed CSOs, including unions, are eligible provided that they have previously received financing at least once for a completed project from an eligible AFD Group entity or through certain qualifying mechanisms. Previous financing may have been received: Directly from the CSO-I mechanism . Through AFD s Operations Directorate. From Expertise France . From Proparco . From the French Facility for Global Environment (FFEM) . From the Fund for Innovation in Development (FID) . Through an FSOF intermediary funding mechanism . From a French embassy , where the annual financing received was more than €100,000. The previous financing may have been received either directly by the locally governed CSO or through a lead CSO , provided the project has been completed. The eligibility requirement applies regardless of the amount of qualifying AFD Group financing received. This means that organizations should carefully review their previous institutional funding history before beginning the application process. Which Countries Are Eligible? The geographical scope of the 2026 AFD CSO call is broad. Countries eligible for the opportunity are countries included on the OECD Development Assistance Committee (DAC) list of ODA recipients . This means that eligibility is not restricted to one particular African subregion or a small group of countries. However, the call gives priority to Least Developed Countries (LDCs) and countries that are particularly vulnerable to climate change. Organizations operating in eligible developing countries should therefore examine how their proposed project responds to development needs, climate vulnerability and other strategic priorities. Projects in France Projects located in France may also be eligible, but under specific programmes: Global Citizenship and International Solidarity Education (ECSI) . Civil Society Capacity Building (SMA) . Organizations proposing projects in France should therefore determine whether their project fits within one of these eligible programmes. What Types of Projects May Be Relevant? The call is intended for projects that contribute to sustainable development, international solidarity, civil society strengthening and concrete benefits for communities. While the supplied call information does not provide a simple list of every eligible thematic sector, applicants should ensure that their proposed initiative clearly connects with the objectives of the CSO Initiatives mechanism and the broader development priorities reflected in the call. Projects are particularly relevant when they: Address clearly identified development challenges. Respond to the needs of beneficiary populations. Demonstrate potential for concrete and measurable impact. Strengthen civil society participation. Contribute to local policy or institutional development. Support sustainable development objectives. Address challenges affecting vulnerable populations. Respond to climate vulnerability where relevant. Demonstrate a strong understanding of the local context. Are designed and led by civil society organizations with appropriate institutional capacity. Important Funding Consideration The 2026 call is a project financing and co-financing opportunity for eligible CSOs . However, the information supplied for this call does not state one universal maximum grant amount that every successful applicant can receive. Applicants should therefore avoid assuming that the programme offers a fixed amount of funding to every organization. Instead, organizations should consult the official call documentation and methodological guide to understand the specific financing arrangements, co-financing requirements and financial conditions applicable to their proposed project. How the Application Process Works The application process is conducted through OSCar , AFD s online platform dedicated to the submission of documents relating to the CSO Initiatives mechanism. Project intentions submitted outside the OSCar platform will not be considered . This makes it important for applicants to begin the administrative process early rather than waiting until the final deadline. Step 1: Confirm organizational eligibility Before preparing the project intention, the organization should determine whether it qualifies under the call. Locally governed CSOs should pay particular attention to the requirement concerning previous qualifying financing and completed projects. Step 2: Review the official call documentation Applicants should carefully read the official call document and methodological guidance. These documents provide important information about the procedures and requirements for preparing and submitting project intentions. Step 3: Prepare an OSCar account CSOs need a user account to access and use OSCar. An authorization to use the platform is required when creating the account. Organizations that already have an OSCar account should ensure that their account remains accessible and that the relevant users have the necessary permissions. Step 4: Request an account if you do not already have one Organizations that do not yet have an OSCar account must submit a request to create their account no later than September 15, 2026 . This is an important administrative deadline because it occurs before the final project submission deadline. Organizations should not interpret October 9 as the only date they need to worry about. Step 5: Prepare the project intention and administrative documents Applicants should prepare the required project intention documentation and supporting administrative documents in accordance with the official templates and guidelines. For locally governed CSOs, AFD provides a specific Project Intention Sheet . Step 6: Submit through OSCar The completed project intention and required administrative documents must be submitted directly through OSCar. Only submissions made through the designated platform will be considered. APPLY HERE Important Application Deadlines There are two important dates to remember for this call. September 15, 2026 — OSCar Account Request Deadline CSOs that do not already have an OSCar account must submit their account creation request by: September 15, 2026 Organizations should therefore start the registration process well before this date. October 9, 2026 — Final Project Submission Deadline The final deadline for submitting project intentions is: October 9, 2026 at 6:00 PM Paris time Applications must be submitted through OSCar before the deadline. Waiting until the final hours could create unnecessary risks, particularly if organizations encounter account, document or technical issues. Documents and Resources Available to Applicants AFD has provided several resources to help CSOs understand and complete the application process. 1. 2026 Call for Expressions of Project Intentions The official call document explains the framework and requirements for the 2026 CSO financing initiative. 2. Project Intention Sheet for Locally Governed CSOs Locally governed CSOs can access the relevant project intention template provided by AFD. 3. Methodological Guide AFD provides a methodological guide explaining the procedures for co-financing projects submitted by French and locally governed CSOs. This guide can help organizations understand the recommended approach to preparing their project intention. 4. Authorization for Use of OSCar Organizations creating an OSCar account need the relevant authorization document. 5. OSCar User Guide AFD also provides a user guide explaining how CSOs can use the OSCar platform and follow the recommended submission procedures. Applicants should make use of these resources before submitting their applications. Why the Opportunity Matters for Civil Society Organizations The AFD CSO call is significant because civil society organizations often have close relationships with communities and can identify challenges that may not always be visible through traditional institutional structures. By recognizing the right of initiative , the mechanism gives eligible organizations an opportunity to propose projects based on their own understanding of development needs. The call can therefore be particularly valuable for CSOs that have: A strong record of community engagement. Experience implementing development projects. Established relationships with local communities. Institutional experience with donor-funded projects. Evidence of previous project results. Capacity to manage project finances and reporting. A clear development or international solidarity mission. A project concept aligned with sustainable development priorities. How to Prepare a Strong Project Intention A competitive project intention should do more than describe a good idea. The organization should demonstrate why the project is necessary, who will benefit, what will be achieved and why the organization is capable of delivering the proposed results. 1. Clearly define the problem Begin by identifying the development challenge the project intends to address. Explain: What the problem is. Who is affected. Where it occurs. Why it matters. What evidence demonstrates the need for intervention. 2. Identify the beneficiaries Clearly describe the populations that will benefit from the proposed project. Where possible, explain the characteristics of the target population and why they require support. 3. Demonstrate local relevance A strong project should be grounded in the realities of the country or community where it will be implemented. Applicants should demonstrate that the organization understands the local context and has meaningful relationships with the communities involved. 4. Explain the proposed solution Describe how the project will respond to the identified problem. The proposed activities should logically connect to the expected results. 5. Demonstrate organizational capacity Applicants should show why their organization is capable of implementing the proposed initiative. Relevant evidence can include: Previous projects. Organizational experience. Staff expertise. Partnerships. Previous donor funding. Community relationships. Previous project results. 6. Connect the project to sustainable development Applicants should demonstrate how the proposed project contributes to relevant Sustainable Development Goals and broader development priorities. 7. Consider climate vulnerability Because the call gives priority to countries particularly vulnerable to climate change, organizations in such contexts should clearly explain relevant climate-related challenges where appropriate. 8. Focus on measurable impact Avoid presenting only activities. Explain the expected changes resulting from the project and how those changes will benefit communities. Key Advantages of the 2026 AFD CSO Call The opportunity offers several important advantages for eligible civil society organizations. Access to Potential Project Financing Selected projects may be considered for AFD financing in 2027, giving eligible organizations an opportunity to secure support for development initiatives. Support for Civil Society The CSO Initiatives mechanism is specifically designed to strengthen civil society stakeholders and their ability to contribute to development. Opportunity for Locally Governed Organizations Eligible locally governed CSOs can potentially access AFD financing under the conditions established by the call. Alignment with Global Development Goals The mechanism is explicitly connected to the Sustainable Development Goals and international solidarity. Potential Policy Impact The initiative is also intended to contribute to local policy, meaning that well-designed projects can potentially influence wider systems and development approaches beyond individual beneficiaries. Important Things Applicants Should Know There are several details that applicants should not overlook. This is not an individual scholarship or fellowship The opportunity is intended for civil society organizations , not individual students, researchers or job seekers. Individuals cannot apply in their personal capacity unless they are applying on behalf of an eligible organization in accordance with the call requirements. Previous financing matters for locally governed CSOs Locally governed organizations should carefully examine the previous-financing requirement before investing substantial time in preparing a submission. The OSCar account deadline comes first Organizations without an existing OSCar account must request one by September 15, 2026 . The final deadline is October 9, 2026 The complete project intention must be submitted by October 9, 2026 at 6:00 PM Paris time . External submissions are not considered Project intentions must be submitted through OSCar. Sending the project through another channel does not satisfy the application requirement. Official Application Platform Eligible organizations should submit their project intention through the official OSCar platform . Access the OSCar application platform Organizations that need to create an account should begin the process as early as possible and observe the September 15, 2026 account-request deadline. For additional guidance, applicants can consult the official AFD call documentation and methodological resources. View the official AFD 2026 CSO Call Contact and Further Assistance Organizations requiring assistance with the OSCar platform can use the official OSCar contact channel provided by AFD. Contact the OSCar team Applicants should also consult the official documentation before contacting the support team, as many procedural questions are addressed in the available guides. Key Facts at a Glance Opportunity 2026 AFD CSO Call for Expressions of Project Intentions Organizer Agence Française de Développement (AFD) Opportunity type CSO project financing / co-financing call Target applicants Eligible civil society organizations Main purpose Support CSO-led development and international solidarity projects Funding year Projects shortlisted for potential financing in 2027 Geographic scope ODA-eligible countries, with priority to LDCs and climate-vulnerable countries French projects Eligible under ECSI and SMA programmes Application platform OSCar OSCar account request deadline September 15, 2026 Final application deadline October 9, 2026 Final submission time 6:00 PM Paris time Application status Ongoing Published July 29, 2026 Frequently Asked Questions What is the 2026 AFD CSO Call for Expressions of Project Intentions? Who can apply? Eligible French CSOs and qualifying locally governed CSOs can apply, subject to the specific requirements of the call. Can individual people apply? Which countries are eligible? All countries eligible for official development assistance according to the OECD DAC list are included, with priority given to Least Developed Countries and countries particularly vulnerable to climate change. Can organizations in France apply? Yes. Projects in France are eligible under the Global Citizenship and International Solidarity Education (ECSI) and Civil Society Capacity Building (SMA) programmes. What is the deadline? The final deadline for submitting project intentions is October 9, 2026 at 6:00 PM Paris time . Is there an earlier deadline? Yes. CSOs that do not already have an OSCar account must request account creation by September 15, 2026 . Where should applications be submitted? Applications must be submitted directly through AFD s OSCar platform. Project intentions submitted through other channels will not be considered. Is the opportunity fully funded? The information provided does not describe the opportunity as a universal fully funded programme or specify one fixed funding amount for every successful applicant. Organizations should consult the official call documents for the applicable financing and co-financing conditions. Visit HERE to learn more about the AFD CSO Call for Expressions of Project Intentions. Final Application Tips Before submitting a project intention, eligible CSOs should consider the following checklist: Confirm that the organization meets the eligibility requirements. If locally governed, verify the previous qualifying financing requirement. Confirm that the proposed country or project location falls within the eligible geographical scope. Review the official 2026 call document carefully. Read the methodological guide. Prepare the required project intention documentation. Ensure that the organization has an active OSCar account. title: ICCROM Fellowships 2027: Apply for a 3–6 Month Cultural Heritage Research Fellowship in Rome
summary: Applications are now open for the ICCROM Fellowship Programme 2027 , offering experienced cultural heritage professionals the opportunity to undertake an independent period of research and study with the International Centre for the Study of the Preservation and Restoration of Cultural Property (ICCROM) . The Fellowship Programme is designed for senior professionals in cultural heritage conservation who want dedicated time to pursue research, exchange knowledge with an international professional community, access ICCROM’s specialist collections, and develop work capable of contributing new perspectives to heritage conservation. Applications for the 2027 cycle opened on: 15 August 2026 and close on: 15 September 2026 Successful Fellowships will normally be undertaken during 2027 , unless another arrangement is agreed with ICCROM. The programme is open to qualified professionals who are nationals of an ICCROM Member State or who work in an organization located in an ICCROM Member State . Applicants must normally have at least a Master’s degree or higher in a field related to cultural heritage and at least 10 years of professional experience in the heritage field . Fellows may undertake research at ICCROM headquarters in Rome, Italy , although a Fellowship may be conducted partly online where there is an appropriate justification. Typical Fellowships last: 3 to 6 months although ICCROM may consider another timeframe where the applicant provides a convincing justification. Applicants should note an important financial condition: ICCROM does not currently provide financial support or a living stipend for Fellows because of budgetary constraints. Fellows are responsible for their own travel, accommodation and personal insurance. ICCROM nevertheless provides important institutional and research support, including office facilities, access to its internationally significant conservation library and archives, internet access and engagement with heritage professionals. About the ICCROM Fellowship Programme The ICCROM Fellowship Programme is an established professional research opportunity intended to enrich the international field of cultural heritage conservation. Its purpose is to: Bring fresh perspectives into ICCROM Facilitate the exchange of knowledge and ideas Encourage new lines of research Strengthen professional relationships Support research relevant to heritage conservation Connect senior professionals with ICCROM resources and expertise The programme is especially appropriate for experienced professionals who already possess substantial knowledge of their field and can independently develop a focused research project. This is not primarily a training course for beginners or an entry-level internship. Fellows are expected to arrive with an independent research agenda and use the period at ICCROM to advance it. What Is ICCROM? ICCROM is an international intergovernmental organization dedicated to the conservation of cultural heritage. Its work involves areas such as: Cultural heritage conservation Heritage risk management Capacity building Research Policy Education Emergency response Collections Sites and monuments Conservation science Heritage management Sustainable development Its international network includes 139 Member States , following San Marino’s accession as the 139th Member State in November 2025. ICCROM’s membership spans countries across Africa, Asia, Europe, the Middle East, the Americas and Oceania. The Fellowship Programme allows experienced researchers and practitioners from this global network to spend time engaging with the organization and its resources. Why Apply for an ICCROM Fellowship? One of the principal advantages of the Fellowship is the opportunity to step away from everyday professional responsibilities and concentrate on independent research in an environment dedicated specifically to cultural heritage. A Fellowship can provide time and space to: Develop an existing research project Investigate a new question Examine archival sources Conduct literature-based research Compare international conservation approaches Develop policy recommendations Strengthen a publication Explore emerging heritage challenges Build international professional relationships The Fellowship is particularly valuable because researchers are placed within an international heritage organization rather than a conventional university department. This creates opportunities to connect academic research with: Conservation practice Policy Institutional experience International cooperation Capacity building Access to One of the World’s Major Conservation Libraries ICCROM highlights its specialist library as one of the most important resources available to Fellows. The collection includes material in more than 70 languages and is regarded as one of the world’s major specialized collections in cultural heritage conservation. Depending on the proposed research, Fellows may use these resources to examine subjects including: Conservation theory Restoration Heritage science Archaeology Museum collections Built heritage Disaster risk Heritage policy Sustainable conservation Education Traditional knowledge Climate-related heritage threats Access to such a specialist collection can be particularly valuable for researchers working on comparative or international projects. Access to ICCROM Archives Fellows also receive access to: ICCROM’s archives where relevant to their research. Archival work can help researchers investigate: The development of international conservation practice Historical heritage policies Institutional cooperation Past ICCROM programmes Training and conservation approaches Evolution of professional standards Applicants whose proposed project depends on specific ICCROM holdings should explain this connection clearly in the research proposal. Research Exchange With ICCROM Professionals The Fellowship is also intended to create opportunities for intellectual exchange. During the Fellowship, participants may interact with: ICCROM staff Other heritage professionals Researchers Practitioners International experts This exchange can help Fellows: Test arguments Receive new perspectives Discover comparative examples Develop future partnerships Identify additional research questions However, applicants must distinguish professional exchange from formal academic supervision. ICCROM Fellows Conduct Independent Research A particularly important condition of the programme is that: Fellows are expected to conduct independent research. Applicants cannot request an ICCROM staff member to serve as their research supervisor. This means candidates should already possess the intellectual and professional experience necessary to: Formulate their own research question Design the research Manage the project independently Analyze material Produce the intended outputs The Fellowship is therefore best suited to established heritage professionals rather than researchers requiring close doctoral-style supervision. Who Can Apply? ICCROM welcomes individuals specializing in disciplines related to: Cultural heritage Applicants may work as: Researchers Teachers Practitioners The Fellowship is particularly aimed at senior professionals. Candidates must satisfy several important requirements. Master s Degree Requirement Applicants must hold at least: A Master’s degree or higher in an area related to cultural heritage. Relevant fields may potentially include areas such as: Conservation Heritage studies Archaeology Architecture Art history Museum studies Conservation science Cultural resource management Historic preservation Anthropology Heritage policy Related disciplines The exact eligibility of a degree depends on its connection to cultural heritage and the applicant’s proposed research. Professional Experience Requirement Candidates must have been professionally active in the cultural heritage field for at least: 10 years This requirement demonstrates clearly that the ICCROM Fellowship is designed for experienced professionals. It is generally not intended for: Recent Bachelor’s graduates Early-stage Master’s students Entry-level heritage workers Professionals with only a few years of relevant experience Applicants should make their professional experience particularly visible in their CV. Geographic Eligibility Applicants must be either: Nationals of an ICCROM Member State , or Professionals working in an organization located within an ICCROM Member State ICCROM’s official membership currently extends across a broad global network of countries. Examples include countries in: Africa Asia Europe North America Latin America and the Caribbean Middle East Oceania Applicants should confirm that their nationality or employer location falls within the official Member States list before applying. Official Member States list: https://www.iccrom.org/about/overview/member-states/full-list Language Requirements Research during the Fellowship may be conducted in: Any language However, Fellows are expected to have good knowledge of at least one of ICCROM’s two official languages: English French This requirement enables Fellows to participate meaningfully in professional exchanges and the institutional life of ICCROM. Applicants should therefore be comfortable communicating professionally in English or French. Research Topics ICCROM welcomes proposals concerning: Any research topic related to cultural heritage conservation and ICCROM’s mission. The call is intentionally broad. Applicants are not required to limit themselves exclusively to the priority themes. However, applications that align strongly with ICCROM’s current Strategic Directions may receive preference during selection. Priority Research Areas for 2026–2027 For the 2026–2027 biennium, ICCROM identifies two particularly important thematic areas. 1. Better Heritage Conservation and Risk Management Approaches ICCROM is interested in research exploring how heritage conservation and risk management can respond more effectively to: Social change Emerging hazards Climate change Urbanization Digital transition Complex crises New technologies This priority reflects the fact that cultural heritage is increasingly exposed to rapidly changing and overlapping risks. Heritage and Climate Change Changing climate patterns create significant risks for heritage. Potential areas of research may include: Extreme weather Flooding Drought Wildfires Sea-level rise Heat Changing humidity Climate-related deterioration Climate adaptation for heritage institutions Risk assessment Researchers might examine both physical threats to heritage and institutional strategies for addressing them. Heritage and Urbanization Rapid urban development can create both opportunities and threats for cultural heritage. Relevant research could potentially address: Historic urban landscapes Development pressure Urban regeneration Infrastructure Community participation Heritage planning Sustainable cities Applicants should link such projects clearly to conservation practice and ICCROM’s mission. Heritage and Digital Transition Digital technologies are rapidly changing how heritage is: Recorded Preserved Interpreted Shared Managed Research could examine areas such as: Digital documentation Artificial intelligence Digital archives Remote sensing 3D technologies Data management Digital access Emerging conservation technologies ICCROM particularly encourages work considering innovative technologies where they contribute to improved conservation and risk management. Heritage in Complex Crises Cultural heritage can be exposed to multiple threats during: Armed conflict Natural disasters Political instability Humanitarian crises Displacement Economic disruption Research may explore how institutions and communities can prepare for, respond to and recover from these situations. Priority Area 2: Integrating Heritage Into Broader Policy Agendas ICCROM also welcomes research examining how heritage can be more effectively incorporated into wider: National and international policy frameworks. This priority recognizes that heritage conservation cannot always operate as a separate policy sector. Instead, heritage increasingly intersects with major policy areas. Heritage and Climate Action Researchers may investigate how heritage can be integrated into: National climate strategies Climate adaptation Climate mitigation Disaster planning International climate policy This can include both protecting heritage from climate impacts and examining how heritage knowledge may contribute to climate resilience. Heritage and Sustainable Development Another major area is the relationship between heritage and: Sustainable development Possible research might examine: Community development Sustainable tourism Cultural industries Local knowledge Urban sustainability Economic development Social resilience Heritage and the Sustainable Development Goals The goal is to better understand how heritage can contribute to development rather than being treated only as an object requiring protection. Heritage and Education ICCROM also identifies: Education as a policy area in which heritage can play an important role. Potential subjects include: Heritage education Youth engagement Professional training Public awareness Heritage in school curricula Community learning Research could investigate how education strengthens conservation while also using heritage as a resource for wider learning. Heritage, Health and Wellbeing ICCROM also highlights connections between heritage and: Health and wellbeing This opens opportunities for research considering: Community identity Mental wellbeing Social cohesion Cultural participation Sense of place Recovery following crisis Applicants should demonstrate how these themes connect meaningfully with cultural heritage conservation. Where Is the Fellowship Based? Fellowships may be undertaken at: ICCROM Headquarters in Rome, Italy Rome offers an especially relevant environment for cultural heritage research because of its concentration of: Conservation institutions Museums Archives Heritage sites Academic organizations International cultural bodies However, the ICCROM Fellowship itself centers on the applicant’s independent research and use of ICCROM’s institutional resources. Partially Online Fellowships A Fellowship may also be conducted: Partially online where the applicant provides an appropriate justification. This does not mean that all applicants should assume the programme can be completed entirely remotely. Applicants seeking a hybrid arrangement should explain clearly: Why partial online participation is necessary Why it remains appropriate for the project How access to ICCROM resources will be managed How the Fellowship objectives will still be achieved Fellowship Duration The normal Fellowship period is: 3 to 6 months This provides Fellows with sufficient time to undertake substantial independent research. However, ICCROM may consider: Alternative timeframes where an applicant provides a convincing justification. Applicants proposing a shorter or longer Fellowship should demonstrate clearly why the research requires that particular schedule. End-of-Fellowship Research Presentation At the end of the Fellowship, Fellows are asked to: Present their research to: ICCROM staff External guests This presentation allows Fellows to communicate: Findings Methods Emerging conclusions Implications for conservation practice Applicants should therefore design projects capable of generating meaningful research outputs within the Fellowship period. Post-Fellowship Feedback After completing the programme, Fellows may be contacted by ICCROM to provide feedback concerning: Their Fellowship experience Research outcomes Professional benefits Wider impact This helps ICCROM assess and improve the Fellowship Programme. Financial Support: Important Information Prospective applicants should pay close attention to the funding arrangements. ICCROM states clearly that: Due to current budgetary constraints, it is not able to provide financial support for Fellowships. Therefore, this is not a funded Fellowship in the traditional sense . ICCROM does not currently provide: A salary Living stipend Travel allowance Accommodation funding Personal insurance funding Applicants should therefore assess carefully whether they can secure: Institutional support Employer funding External research funding Personal funding before committing to a residential Fellowship in Rome. What Fellows Must Pay For Fellows are responsible for arranging and financing: Travel Applicants must organize travel to and from Italy. Accommodation Fellows must pay for their accommodation. ICCROM may assist, where possible, in identifying reasonably priced accommodation, but accommodation itself is not funded. Personal Insurance Fellows must arrange their own insurance. The programme requires: Valid major global medical and accident insurance for the entire Fellowship period. This is compulsory. Visa Support Although ICCROM does not pay travel or visa-related living costs, it can assist successful Fellows with obtaining documents required to: Enter Italy Temporarily reside in Italy This institutional support can help Fellows navigate immigration procedures. Applicants remain responsible for ensuring they comply with applicable Italian entry and residence requirements. What ICCROM Provides Although there is no financial stipend, ICCROM provides substantial research infrastructure. During the Fellowship, participants receive: Office space Computer workstation Unlimited internet access Stationery Documentation services Library access Archive access For established researchers who already have external financial support, these institutional resources may make the Fellowship particularly valuable. How to Apply Applications are submitted using ICCROM’s: Online Fellowship Research Proposal Application form The application form is available during the application period beginning on: 15 August 2026 Applicants should complete all required sections and upload supporting documentation before the deadline. APPLY HERE Required Application Documents Applicants need several digital files. The accepted file formats include: PDF DOC DOCX JPG JPEG PNG TIF TIFF Each file must have a maximum size of: 3 MB The required supporting documentation includes three main components. 1. Updated Curriculum Vitae Applicants must provide an: Up-to-date CV The CV should demonstrate: Academic qualifications Professional history Heritage specialization Research experience Publications Teaching Conservation work Major projects International experience Other relevant achievements Given the 10-year professional experience requirement, applicants should make their seniority and heritage expertise immediately clear. 2. Employer Agreement Where applicable, applicants must provide: Confirmation from their employer agreeing to the research period at ICCROM. This is especially relevant for applicants currently employed by: Universities Museums Heritage agencies Government institutions NGOs Conservation organizations The document should demonstrate that the employer understands and supports the applicant’s proposed absence or research activity. 3. Three Letters of Reference Applicants must provide: Three letters of reference from people who have: Direct knowledge of the applicant’s work. Referees should therefore be capable of commenting credibly on: Professional expertise Research ability Conservation experience Independence Contribution to the heritage field Suitability for the proposed project Applicants should contact referees well before September 15. What If You Cannot Use the Online Application Form? Applicants unable to submit their materials through the online system may contact the Fellowship Programme focal point. Contact: Alison Heritage Project Manager, Strategic Planning and Research ICCROM – Fellowship Programme Via di San Michele, 13 I-00153 Rome, Italy Email: fellowships@iccrom.org Fax: +39 06 58 55 33 49 Applicants should contact ICCROM before the deadline if technical or accessibility issues prevent normal online submission. Fellowship Selection Process Applications are assessed by the: Fellowship Selection Committee Candidates will be informed of the Committee’s decision in writing once results are available. ICCROM does not provide a fixed notification date because the timeframe can vary depending on the number of applications received. How Applications Are Evaluated ICCROM publishes six major selection criteria. Understanding these criteria can help applicants prepare much stronger proposals. 1. Overall Quality and Clarity The proposed research should be: Clearly written Logically organized Well defined Intellectually coherent Avoid overly broad topics. A three-to-six-month Fellowship requires a focused research question. 2. Research Need The project should address an: Identified knowledge gap. Applicants should therefore explain: What is already known What remains unclear Why the gap matters Why additional research is needed A proposal that simply summarizes an established topic will likely be less competitive. 3. Quality of Anticipated Results Applicants should demonstrate how their expected findings will represent: A useful development A practical contribution Intellectual progress A meaningful advance for the field of heritage conservation. Results might potentially take forms such as: Academic paper Policy recommendations Methodological framework Professional guidelines Comparative analysis Research report Applicants should be specific about anticipated outputs. 4. Feasibility ICCROM evaluates whether the proposed research can realistically be completed using: Available resources ICCROM collections Fellowship timeframe Applicant expertise A highly ambitious project requiring several years of fieldwork would probably not be appropriate for a three-to-six-month Fellowship unless the ICCROM period forms a clearly defined component of a larger project. 5. Dissemination Plan Applicants must explain how their research findings will be shared with the: Broader heritage conservation community. Possible dissemination routes may include: Open-access publication Academic journal Conference presentation Professional workshop Institutional briefing Online resources Training materials Policy communication ICCROM particularly encourages: Open-access dissemination. 6. Relevance to ICCROM s Strategic Directions Applications connected with ICCROM’s current Strategic Directions receive preference. For 2026–2027, candidates should pay particular attention to the priority themes concerning: Heritage risk management Climate change Urbanization Digital transition Complex crises Innovative technologies Heritage and climate policy Sustainable development Education Health and wellbeing A proposal does not necessarily need to fit these themes to qualify, but a strong connection can improve strategic relevance. Preparing a Competitive ICCROM Fellowship Proposal 1. Identify a Specific Conservation Problem Avoid proposing a topic such as: “Climate Change and Cultural Heritage.” Instead, narrow it to: A particular heritage type Specific geographic context Defined risk Policy problem Methodological issue A focused question is easier to complete within the Fellowship period. 2. Explain Why ICCROM Is Necessary Do not write a proposal that could just as easily be completed at home. Explain what ICCROM offers that is particularly valuable. This might include: Specialist library holdings Archives International conservation literature Institutional history Comparative expertise Professional exchange 3. Demonstrate Professional Experience The programme requires at least 10 years in the heritage field. Use your application to show how that experience positions you to undertake genuinely independent research. 4. Connect Research With Practice ICCROM is strongly practice-oriented. Where appropriate, explain how your research can improve: Conservation approaches Risk management Policy Professional practice Institutional capacity Community engagement 5. Build a Realistic Research Schedule A strong proposal should demonstrate what will happen during each phase of the Fellowship. For example: Initial literature and archive review Comparative analysis Consultation and professional exchange Drafting Validation Final output preparation 6. Develop a Strong Dissemination Plan Do not leave dissemination as an afterthought. Explain: Who needs your findings How you will reach them Which platforms you will use Whether materials will be open access How the work can continue beyond the Fellowship 7. Prepare Your Funding Plan Because ICCROM does not provide a stipend, applicants should consider funding before applying. Potential routes may include: Employer support University research funds External grants Professional development funds National heritage institutions Personal resources The absence of ICCROM financial support should be factored into the feasibility of the Fellowship. Important Details at a Glance Organisation: ICCROM Programme: ICCROM Fellowship Programme Cycle: 2027 Application opening: 15 August 2026 Application deadline: 15 September 2026 Fellowship year: 2027 Normal duration: 3–6 months Location: ICCROM Headquarters, Rome, Italy Hybrid option: Partial online participation possible with justification Target applicants: Senior cultural heritage professionals Minimum qualification: Master’s degree or higher in a cultural heritage-related area Professional experience: Minimum 10 years Language: Good knowledge of English or French Research language: Any language Financial stipend: None Travel: Applicant responsibility Accommodation: Applicant responsibility Insurance: Applicant responsibility and mandatory Office space: Provided Computer workstation: Provided Internet: Provided Library and archive access: Provided References: Three letters Employer approval: Required where applicable Official programme information: https://www.iccrom.org/get-involved/fellowships Conclusion The ICCROM Fellowship Programme 2027 offers an important research opportunity for senior cultural heritage professionals who want to spend dedicated time developing independent research while engaging with one of the world’s leading international organizations for heritage conservation. The programme welcomes researchers, teachers and practitioners working across cultural heritage disciplines. Applicants must normally hold at least a Master’s degree in a heritage-related field and have at least 10 years of professional experience . Research may address any topic connected with cultural heritage conservation and ICCROM’s mission. However, the 2026–2027 cycle gives particular preference to projects addressing improved conservation and risk-management approaches, climate change, urbanization, digital transition, complex crises and innovative technologies, as well as research integrating heritage into climate action, sustainable development, education, health and wellbeing. Fellowships normally last three to six months and may be undertaken at ICCROM headquarters in Rome, with partial online arrangements possible when justified. Fellows receive office space, a workstation, internet access and full use of ICCROM’s specialist documentation, library and archives. ICCROM’s conservation library includes holdings in more than 70 languages. Applicants should nevertheless understand that this is currently a self-funded Fellowship . ICCROM does not provide a stipend, travel allowance or accommodation funding because of present budget constraints. Fellows must arrange and finance their own travel, accommodation and mandatory medical and accident insurance. The application requires an updated CV, employer approval where applicable and three reference letters from people with direct knowledge of the applicant’s work. title: UNIDIR Graduate Professional Programme 2026 in Geneva: $1,500 Monthly Stipend for Graduate Students and Recent Graduates
summary: The United Nations Institute for Disarmament Research (UNIDIR) is inviting applications for its Graduate Professional position in Integrated Approaches – Gender and Disarmament in Geneva, Switzerland. The opportunity provides graduate students and eligible recent graduates with the chance to gain practical professional experience within a United Nations institution while contributing to research and programme activities focused on disarmament, international peace and security, gender, and youth engagement . The Graduate Professional will work within UNIDIR s Integrated Approaches – Gender and Disarmament Programme , supporting research, programme implementation, communication, coordination and administrative activities. The position is particularly suited to candidates interested in international relations, political science, international law, gender studies, disarmament, arms control, youth engagement and United Nations affairs. The position is based in Geneva , is full-time, and is expected to begin in November 2026 . The programme will run for six months , with the possibility of extension, and successful candidates will receive a USD 1,500 monthly stipend as a contribution towards living expenses in Geneva. The application deadline is September 16, 2026, at midnight Geneva time . UNIDIR Graduate Professional Programme 2026 at a Glance Detail Information Organization United Nations Institute for Disarmament Research (UNIDIR) Position Graduate Professional Programme Integrated Approaches – Gender and Disarmament Location Geneva, Switzerland Starting date November 2026 Duration 6 months, with possibility of extension Working rate 100% full-time Stipend USD 1,500 per month Application deadline September 16, 2026 Deadline time Midnight Geneva time Experience required Professional work experience is not required Language Fluency in English required Application method Email application in PDF format Application email unidir.recruitment@un.org Subject line UNIDIR GPP – IntApp (Geneva) About the United Nations Institute for Disarmament Research The United Nations Institute for Disarmament Research (UNIDIR) is a voluntarily funded and autonomous institution within the United Nations system. UNIDIR is one of the few policy research institutes in the world dedicated specifically to issues surrounding disarmament and international security . Based in Geneva, the institute conducts research, generates knowledge and facilitates dialogue and action on critical security challenges. Its work helps the international community develop practical and innovative approaches to some of the most important issues affecting global peace and security. The Graduate Professional opportunity therefore provides an opportunity to gain experience in an international policy environment while working alongside professionals engaged in research, multilateral affairs and disarmament-related programmes. About the Integrated Approaches – Gender and Disarmament Programme The Graduate Professional will work within UNIDIR s Integrated Approaches – Gender and Disarmament Programme . The programme focuses on generating policy-relevant knowledge and providing multilateral practitioners with practical tools that can help them incorporate a gender perspective into their work . The programme also supports youth engagement across different areas of arms control and disarmament . This makes the position particularly relevant for candidates who want to explore the connections between: Gender and international security. Youth and disarmament. Arms control. International peace and security. Multilateral diplomacy. United Nations policy. International relations. Political science. International law. Gender studies. Conventional arms control. Policy research and analysis. What Will the Graduate Professional Do? The selected Graduate Professional will support the work of the Integrated Approaches – Gender and Disarmament Programme under the supervision of the Head of Programme. The responsibilities combine research, programme support, communications, coordination and administrative work. 1. Conduct Background Research One of the central responsibilities will be conducting background research to support the programme s activities. This may involve gathering relevant information, reviewing existing materials, identifying useful evidence and helping programme staff prepare for research and policy activities. Candidates should therefore be comfortable with research, information gathering and analytical work. 2. Support Programme Activities The Graduate Professional will assist with planning and implementing programme activities. These activities may include: Meetings. Workshops. Conferences. Field missions. Other programme-related activities. This responsibility provides practical exposure to how international programmes are organized and delivered. 3. Support Communication and Coordination The position also involves day-to-day communication and coordination responsibilities. The successful candidate may be required to help ensure that information is communicated effectively, stakeholders are coordinated and programme activities are properly organized. Strong written and oral communication skills are therefore important. 4. Provide Administrative Support The Graduate Professional will also contribute to administrative tasks required by programme staff. Applicants should therefore be comfortable managing multiple responsibilities, keeping track of deadlines and supporting organizational processes. 5. Perform Other Programme-Related Tasks The Graduate Professional may be assigned other tasks as required by programme staff. This means that adaptability and willingness to support different aspects of the programme will be important. Key Skills and Interests Required UNIDIR is looking for a candidate with a combination of research, communication, organizational and technical skills. Research and Presentation Skills Applicants should demonstrate strong research and presentation abilities. The role requires the ability to gather information, understand complex issues and communicate findings effectively. Strong Writing and Synthesis Skills The Graduate Professional should be able to transform information into concise, high-quality written briefs . This is particularly important in an international policy environment, where large amounts of information often need to be synthesized into clear and useful documents. Organizational and Coordination Skills The position requires the ability to manage multiple tasks and responsibilities. United Nations work. Candidates with an academic or professional interest in these areas may be particularly well suited to the opportunity. UN Core Values and Required Competencies The Graduate Professional is expected to demonstrate the core values of the United Nations. Communication The successful candidate should be able to identify the information needs of different audiences and adapt communication accordingly. This includes: Writing clearly and concisely. Monitor progress. Adjust plans when necessary. Ensure that assignments are completed effectively. Creativity UNIDIR also values creativity and innovative thinking. Location of the Programme The Graduate Professional position is based in Geneva, Switzerland . title: Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation Scholarship 2027: Fully Funded PhD Scholarship in Canada for International and Canadian Students
summary: The Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation Scholarship 2027 is now accepting applications from exceptional doctoral students whose research falls broadly within the humanities and social sciences and addresses important issues relevant to Canada and the wider world. The prestigious doctoral scholarship provides substantial financial support, research and travel funding, mentorship, experiential learning opportunities, and access to a multidisciplinary community of Scholars, Fellows, Mentors, and alumni. For the 2027 competition, applicants must first complete an eligibility verification process before they can access the full scholarship application. The deadline to request eligibility confirmation is October 2, 2026 , while the final application deadline is November 6, 2026, at 4:00 p.m. ET . Opportunity Overview Opportunity: Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation PhD Scholarship 2027 Category: Scholarship Study level: PhD/Doctoral Fields: Humanities and Social Sciences Study location: Canada, with specific eligibility provisions for Canadian students studying abroad Scholarship duration: Three years Annual stipend: Up to $50,000 Research, networking and travel allowance: Up to $20,000 per year Eligibility verification deadline: October 2, 2026 Reference deadline: October 30, 2026, at 9:00 a.m. ET Complete application deadline: November 6, 2026, at 4:00 p.m. ET Application process: Two steps Official organization: Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation About the Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation Scholarship The Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation PhD Scholarship is designed to support outstanding doctoral researchers whose work can contribute to important conversations and challenges affecting Canada and society. The Foundation is not simply looking for students with excellent grades. Its selection approach considers the broader potential of applicants, including their intellectual curiosity, leadership potential, engagement with society, ability to communicate knowledge, and capacity to create meaningful impact beyond academia. Successful Scholars become part of a multidisciplinary community where academic research is connected with public dialogue, mentorship, experiential learning, networking, and societal engagement. This makes the opportunity particularly relevant for doctoral students who want their research to have an influence beyond academic publications and contribute to wider discussions about major social, environmental, political, cultural, and human challenges. Scholarship Benefits One of the major attractions of the Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation Scholarship is its combination of financial support and professional development. 1. Annual stipend of up to $50,000 Selected Scholars can receive up to $50,000 per year for three years to support tuition and living expenses associated with their doctoral studies. Over the three-year scholarship period, this represents potential stipend support of up to $150,000 . The funding is intended to give doctoral researchers greater financial stability while they concentrate on their studies and research. 2. Research, networking and travel allowance Scholars can also receive up to $20,000 per year for three years to support activities connected to their doctoral work. This allowance can help support: Research-related activities Academic and professional travel Networking Participation in relevant events Activities connected with Foundation programming Other research-related opportunities This additional funding can be particularly valuable for researchers whose projects require fieldwork, conferences, collaboration, or engagement beyond their home institution. 3. Mentorship and experiential learning The scholarship goes beyond financial assistance by providing Scholars with opportunities to engage with Mentors and Fellows. The Foundation s programming can include: Meetings Masterclasses Seminars Conferences Leadership development Experiential learning Interdisciplinary exchanges Public policy discussions These opportunities are designed to broaden Scholars perspectives and help them connect their academic research with practical societal challenges. 4. Multidisciplinary community Successful applicants become part of a community involving Scholars, Fellows and Mentors working across different disciplines and sectors. This community can provide opportunities to: Exchange ideas across academic disciplines Develop professional relationships Learn from experienced researchers and leaders Share research with broader audiences Explore interdisciplinary approaches Participate in conversations about major societal issues 5. Alumni network Scholars also become part of the Foundation s alumni network, which includes more than 500 alumni . This creates a long-term professional and intellectual network that can continue beyond the three-year scholarship period. Fields of Study and Research Themes Applicants must be pursuing doctoral research broadly related to the humanities or social sciences . However, being in one of these broad academic fields is not enough. The proposed PhD research must also address issues relevant to Canada s future and align with at least one of the Foundation s four foundational themes . The four themes are: 1. Human Rights and Dignity This theme focuses on issues surrounding human rights, dignity, equality, justice, inclusion, and the conditions necessary for individuals and communities to live with dignity. Potential research areas may include questions related to: Human rights Social justice Equality Inclusion Discrimination Rights and freedoms Vulnerable populations Human dignity 2. Responsible Citizenship This theme concerns citizenship, participation, democratic life, civic engagement, and the responsibilities individuals and institutions have within society. Research connected to this theme may explore: Democracy Civic participation Citizenship Governance Political engagement Social responsibility Community participation Public institutions 3. Canada and the World This theme examines Canada s relationship with the international community and Canada s role in global affairs. Relevant research could address: International relations Globalization Diplomacy Migration International development Global governance Canada s international role Cross-border social and political issues 4. People and Their Natural Environment This theme explores relationships between people, society and the natural environment. Potential research areas may include: Environmental policy Climate change Sustainability Environmental justice Human-environment relationships Natural resource governance Ecological challenges Sustainable development Applicants should therefore ensure that their research proposal clearly demonstrates how their doctoral project connects with at least one of these four themes. Who Can Apply for the 2027 Scholarship? The Foundation has established specific citizenship and enrollment requirements. Eligible applicants must fall into one of three categories : Canadian students enrolled at a Canadian university Canadian students enrolled at a university outside Canada International students enrolled at a Canadian university This means international students can apply, but they must be enrolled in a doctoral program at a Canadian university . Importantly, international students who are residing outside Canada and enrolled at a university outside Canada are not eligible for this particular scholarship. Therefore, applicants should carefully distinguish between citizenship and university enrollment when determining eligibility. PhD Stage Requirements The 2027 scholarship is specifically targeted at early-stage doctoral researchers. At the time of application, candidates must be either: In the first year of their PhD program , or In the second year of their PhD program . Applicants who are beyond the second year of their doctoral program should therefore carefully assess whether they meet the Foundation s requirements before beginning the application. There is no age limit for applying to the scholarship. What Does the Foundation Look For? Academic excellence is important, but the Foundation evaluates applicants more broadly. The strongest candidates are expected to demonstrate several qualities. Academic Excellence Applicants should have an outstanding academic record and demonstrate strong intellectual ability. Academic performance is assessed across the application, including: Academic transcripts Research proposal Letters of recommendation Overall application quality The Foundation states that successful applicants stand out through the quality of their research and their academic excellence. Intellectual Curiosity The Foundation seeks doctoral researchers who demonstrate genuine curiosity and an ambition to explore important questions. Your application should therefore demonstrate not only what you are researching, but also: Why the question matters What makes the research intellectually significant What knowledge gap you are addressing What new perspectives your work could contribute Leadership Potential Applicants should demonstrate potential to contribute positively beyond their immediate academic environment. Leadership does not necessarily have to mean holding a formal leadership position. It can be demonstrated through: Community initiatives Research collaborations Advocacy Professional activities Student leadership Public engagement Projects that have produced meaningful results Commitment to Society The Foundation places considerable emphasis on applicants who are interested in connecting research with society. Strong applications should show how the applicant s work could contribute to broader conversations or help address significant societal challenges. Potential for Impact Beyond Academia Applicants should think carefully about how their research can reach audiences outside universities. This could involve: Public policy Communities Civil society Government Professional organizations Practitioners Public education Knowledge translation The Foundation specifically emphasizes the importance of sharing knowledge and creating meaningful impact beyond academia. Collaboration and Knowledge Sharing The Foundation also values applicants who are willing to engage in dialogue, interdisciplinary collaboration, and knowledge exchange. A strong candidate should therefore be able to demonstrate an openness to learning from people working in other disciplines and sectors. Letters of Reference Applicants must provide three letters of reference . The three referees must include: One PhD supervisor One additional academic referee One referee from outside academia The inclusion of a non-academic referee is particularly important because the Foundation is interested in applicants broader engagement and potential impact beyond academia. Applicants should therefore select referees strategically rather than simply choosing individuals based on academic seniority. A good referee should ideally be able to provide specific evidence of your: Academic ability Research potential Leadership Community or professional engagement Communication skills Commitment to societal impact Potential for future contribution How the 2027 Application Process Works The 2027 competition introduces a two-step application process . Step 1: Eligibility Verification Applicants must first complete a short eligibility verification form. This initial step allows the Foundation to confirm whether an applicant meets the scholarship s eligibility requirements. The eligibility verification request must be submitted by: October 2, 2026. Applicants should not wait until the final day if they can avoid it. Reviewing the eligibility requirements in advance can help identify potential problems before submission. Step 2: Full Scholarship Application Only applicants whose eligibility has been confirmed will receive access to the full application form. This means applicants cannot simply skip the eligibility verification stage and proceed directly to the full application . The Foundation states that applications that do not meet the eligibility criteria will not be reviewed. Important 2027 Scholarship Deadlines Applicants should keep track of all dates rather than focusing only on the final application deadline. September 1, 2026 The 2027 application process opens, including the eligibility verification form. October 2, 2026 Deadline to submit an eligibility confirmation request. This is the first major deadline and should not be confused with the final application deadline. Weeks of October 5 and October 12, 2026 Mandatory information sessions. Eligible applicants should pay attention to instructions from the Foundation regarding participation in these sessions. October 30, 2026 — 9:00 a.m. ET Deadline for all three reference letters to be received. Applicants should contact referees well in advance because the letters must be received by the deadline. November 6, 2026 — 4:00 p.m. ET Final deadline for submitting the complete scholarship application. How to Prepare a Strong Application Because the scholarship is highly selective, applicants should approach the application strategically. 1. Confirm Your Eligibility Early Before investing significant time in the application, check: Your citizenship status Your university s location Your current PhD year Your field of study Your research topic Your alignment with the four Foundation themes This is especially important for international applicants because international students must be enrolled at a Canadian university. 2. Develop a Clear Research Narrative Your research proposal should make it easy for reviewers to understand: The problem you are investigating Why the problem matters The research gap Your research questions Your approach The expected contribution The relevance of your work to Canada and society How your research connects to the Foundation s themes Avoid presenting your project as merely an academic exercise. Explain why the research matters in the real world. 3. Clearly Connect Your Research to a Foundation Theme Do not assume reviewers will automatically see the connection. Explicitly explain how your research relates to one or more of: Human Rights and Dignity Responsible Citizenship Canada and the World People and their Natural Environment A well-developed thematic connection can help demonstrate that your project fits the Foundation s objectives. 4. Demonstrate Impact Think beyond publications and academic conferences. Explain how your research could potentially influence: Public policy Communities Institutions Professional practice Public understanding Social debates Government decision-making 5. Choose Your Referees Carefully Because three references are required and one must come from outside academia, applicants should begin approaching potential referees early. Give referees sufficient information about: Your research The scholarship Your achievements Your goals The Foundation s themes Why you believe you are a strong candidate This makes it easier for referees to write detailed and relevant recommendations. 6. Demonstrate Engagement Beyond Academia If you have participated in community projects, professional initiatives, policy discussions, advocacy, public communication, volunteering, or other activities related to your research, explain their relevance. The Foundation is interested in researchers who can connect knowledge with society. APPLY HERE Why This Scholarship Is Different from a Conventional PhD Scholarship Many doctoral scholarships primarily focus on financial support. The Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation Scholarship combines financial assistance with an extensive intellectual and professional development component. The Foundation describes its scholarship as more than financial support, emphasizing mentorship, experiential learning, community engagement and knowledge sharing. A Scholar therefore gains access to: Substantial doctoral funding Research and travel support Mentorship Leadership opportunities Interdisciplinary discussions Experiential learning Professional networking A multidisciplinary community A long-term alumni network For doctoral students interested in connecting academic research with real-world challenges, this broader model can be particularly valuable. Frequently Asked Questions Can international students apply? Yes. International students are eligible if they are enrolled in a doctoral program at a Canadian university . International students residing outside Canada and enrolled at universities outside Canada are not eligible. Can Canadian students studying outside Canada apply? Yes. Canadian students enrolled at universities outside Canada can apply, provided they meet the other eligibility requirements. Can students in their third year of a PhD apply? No. For the 2027 competition, applicants must be in their first or second year of doctoral studies at the time of application . Is there an age limit? No. The Foundation states that there is no age limit for applicants. Do applicants have to speak both English and French? No. Applicants do not need to be fluent in both official languages. However, they must be able to communicate effectively in either English or French . How much is the scholarship worth? The scholarship provides up to $50,000 per year for three years , plus up to $20,000 per year for research, networking and travel . Is the scholarship renewable? The scholarship is structured as a three-year program . Can Scholars receive other scholarships? Yes, but the Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation Scholarship may be adjusted depending on funding received from other organizations, universities or institutions. Scholars must declare additional sources of income each year. The Foundation states that, regardless of other funding, Scholars continue to receive the annual research allowance, while the annual stipend has a minimum level of $25,000. Application Link Applicants should begin by reviewing the official eligibility requirements and then completing the eligibility verification process. Applicants with questions about the 2027 scholarship can contact the Foundation at scholarship2027@trudeaufoundation.ca . Visit HERE to learn more about the Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation Scholarship 2027. Conclusion The Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation Scholarship 2027 is a major opportunity for early-stage doctoral researchers in the humanities and social sciences who want to combine academic excellence with leadership, public engagement and meaningful societal impact. The scholarship offers up to $50,000 annually for three years , an additional $20,000 per year for research, networking and travel , mentorship, experiential learning, interdisciplinary engagement and access to a community of more than 500 alumni. However, applicants should pay close attention to the eligibility requirements. The opportunity is open to Canadian students studying in Canada or abroad, as well as international students enrolled at Canadian universities. Applicants must also be in the first or second year of their PhD and their research must fall broadly within the humanities or social sciences while aligning with at least one of the Foundation s four themes. The first critical deadline is October 2, 2026 , when applicants must submit their eligibility confirmation request. Those who pass the eligibility stage must then ensure their three references are received by October 30, 2026 , and submit the complete application by November 6, 2026, at 4:00 p.m. ET . For prospective Scholars, the key to a competitive application is not simply demonstrating strong academic performance. Applicants should present a compelling research project, clearly articulate its relevance to Canada and society, demonstrate leadership and engagement, and show how their work can create impact beyond academia.
