What Is the Brooke Owens Fellowship? The Brooke Owens Fellowship was created to expand opportunities for undergraduate women and gender minorities who want to become leaders, innovators and contributors within aerospace. The program is named in honor of Dawn Brooke Owens , an accomplished aerospace professional and pilot whose career included work connected with NASA s Johnson Space Center, the XPRIZE Foundation, the Federal Aviation Administration s Office of Commercial Space Transportation and the White House Office of Management and Budget. The initiative was founded by aerospace leaders who knew Brooke personally and wanted to create opportunities for a new generation of people who could bring similar talent, creativity, determination and commitment to service into the industry. Today, the program focuses on providing career opportunities, mentorship, professional development, industry connections and a strong community for undergraduate women and gender-minority students interested in aerospace. The organization is a U.S.-registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit and has developed a substantial network of aerospace professionals, executives, mentors, host organizations and alumni. Applications for the Class of 2027 Are Now Open The Class of 2027 represents the 11th group of Brooke Owens Fellows , marking more than a decade since the program s first fellowship class. Applications opened on September 1 and will remain open until October 4, 2026. The latest official announcement confirms that the opportunity is available to women and gender-minority undergraduate students from all college majors who are interested in careers in aerospace and aviation. This broad academic approach is important because aerospace is much larger than aerospace engineering alone. Professionals working in the sector may come from backgrounds including: Aerospace engineering Mechanical engineering Electrical engineering Computer science Artificial intelligence Data science Physics Mathematics Chemistry Biology Earth and environmental sciences Business Finance Communications Public relations Art and design Law Public policy International affairs Government Education STEM outreach The program s FAQ explicitly states that applicants do not have to major in aerospace engineering . Students from engineering, science, business, communications, art, law, policy and other academic fields may apply if they are seriously interested in building a career in aerospace. What Will Selected Brooke Owens Fellows Receive? The Brooke Owens Fellowship combines industry exposure with mentorship, community and professional development. For the Class of 2027, the official announcement states that successful Fellows will: Participate in a summer internship with a host company. Receive one-on-one mentorship from professionals aligned with their areas of interest. Attend a professional development summit with the other Fellows in their class. The Brooke Owens Fellowship also describes its broader program as providing access to paid internships and executive-level mentorship from senior aerospace figures, including executives, astronauts and industry leaders. Summer Aerospace Industry Experience A major element of the program is meaningful exposure to the aerospace industry. The 2027 program announcement states that accepted Fellows will participate in a summer internship at a host company . This provides students with the opportunity to move from classroom learning into professional aerospace environments and develop practical experience in the sector. Past Fellows have worked across areas such as: Rocket propulsion Satellite operations Mission planning Aerospace policy STEM outreach Engineering Software Space systems Research Communications Other aerospace-related functions. The fellowship is therefore relevant not only to students pursuing highly technical engineering careers but also to those interested in the business, policy, communications and social dimensions of aerospace. One-on-One Professional Mentorship Mentorship is another central feature of the Brooke Owens Fellowship. Each Fellow is connected with experienced professionals who can provide guidance as the Fellow enters or develops within the aerospace sector. The Fellowship s current mentor structure pairs Fellows with hand-selected mentors, with relationships beginning before Fellows start their summer positions. Mentors support Fellows as they prepare for professional roles, navigate workplace challenges and make decisions about their longer-term careers. Many mentor relationships reportedly continue beyond the official summer program. The program s mentors have included senior aerospace professionals, astronauts, executives, engineers and other industry leaders. For a university student preparing to enter a highly specialized sector, this kind of direct professional access can help with: Career planning. Understanding aerospace industry pathways. Developing professional networks. Navigating early-career decisions. Preparing for internships and employment. Learning directly from experienced aerospace leaders. Building professional confidence. Identifying future areas of specialization. Brooke Owens Professional Development Summit Selected Fellows also participate in the annual Brooke Owens Summit , which brings members of the fellowship class together for professional development. The 2027 announcement confirms that successful Fellows will attend a professional development summit alongside their cohort. The summit adds an important cohort component to the program. Rather than completing an internship independently, Fellows become part of a community of students pursuing careers across different parts of aerospace. This can create valuable relationships that continue as participants move into graduate education, industry, government, entrepreneurship, research and other aerospace careers. A Long-Term Aerospace Community The Fellowship is designed to create more than a one-summer experience. The official Class of 2027 application describes Fellows as joining a lasting community of: Peers. Mentors. Aerospace professionals. Industry leaders. This community-based model can be particularly valuable in aerospace, where professional relationships, specialized knowledge and industry networks can play an important role in career development. The goal stated by the program is not simply to help students obtain their first aerospace opportunity, but to help develop people who may eventually shape the future direction of the industry. More Than 400 Fellows Have Joined the Program The Brooke Owens Fellowship has grown significantly since its creation. According to the program s September 2026 announcement: 418 undergraduate students have been accepted since the program began. Fellows have come from nearly 40 U.S. states and territories . Participants have represented 10 countries . 124 companies have hosted Fellows for summer internships. 105 mentors have helped support Fellows during their early careers. Fellows have represented 147 schools . These figures demonstrate that the fellowship has developed into an established pathway connecting undergraduate talent with the aerospace industry. Detailed Eligibility Requirements Before beginning an application, candidates should carefully confirm that they satisfy every current requirement. The official Class of 2027 application page lists four principal eligibility conditions. 1. You Must Be an Undergraduate Student Applicants must currently be undergraduate students. They must have completed at least one year of coursework toward a bachelor s or associate degree by the time they apply. This means the program is aimed at students who have progressed beyond the very beginning of their undergraduate education. 2. You Must Be Interested in an Aerospace Career Applicants must demonstrate genuine interest in pursuing a career in the aerospace industry. Engineering and non-engineering career pathways are both accepted. Candidates therefore should not assume that admission is restricted to: Aerospace engineers. Mechanical engineers. Scientists. Technical majors. Students from other disciplines are encouraged to apply when they can demonstrate a credible connection between their interests and an aerospace career. 3. Applicants Must Identify as a Woman or Gender Minority The Fellowship is specifically designed to increase opportunities for people underrepresented in aerospace because of gender. The formal Class of 2027 eligibility criteria require applicants to identify as a woman or gender minority . The organization s FAQ specifically notes that this includes women and other gender minorities, including nonbinary and gender-nonconforming individuals. 4. Applicants Must Be at Least 18 Applicants must be 18 years of age or older . Students From All Academic Majors Can Apply One of the strongest features of the Brooke Owens Fellowship is that it recognizes the multidisciplinary nature of aerospace. Students do not have to study aerospace engineering. The official FAQ specifically welcomes applicants from academic backgrounds such as engineering, science, business, communications, art, law and policy, along with other disciplines. The critical factor is whether the applicant has a genuine ambition to build a career and create an impact within aerospace. Is There a Minimum GPA? No minimum GPA is stated. The Fellowship deliberately uses a broader approach to identifying talent. The official application guidance notes that past Fellows have included students with very high GPAs as well as students whose academic records were considerably lower. The organization states that GPA represents only one imperfect way of assessing an applicant s abilities and potential. The FAQ similarly states that applications are reviewed holistically, with consideration given to factors including the applicant s: Personal statement. Creative submission. Recommendation. Character. Leadership. Creativity. Service. Alignment with Fellowship values. Students should therefore not automatically rule themselves out because they do not have a perfect academic record. Documents You Need to Prepare The application requires several supporting materials. Applicants should start preparing these well before the October deadline because the process includes both conventional application documents and original creative work. Updated Resume or CV Applicants need their most recent resume or CV. The Fellowship recommends making sure the document is accurate, polished and carefully proofread. Relevant experience may include: Academic activities. Internships. Paid employment. Volunteer activities. Independent projects. Leadership positions. Clubs. Extracurricular activities. Relevant community involvement. Applicants should use the resume to show not merely academic performance but evidence that they could contribute effectively as a teammate and member of the aerospace community. Academic Transcript Applicants must submit their latest transcript. Importantly, an unofficial transcript is acceptable , and the Fellowship actually encourages students to use unofficial versions when obtaining an official transcript would require paying a fee. The transcript submitted must contain completed, graded coursework. The application guidance says it needs to include at least one full semester of completed grades , rather than only midterm results. Applicants studying at a new institution who do not yet have an appropriate transcript there may use a transcript from their previous institution where applicable. Note that the formal Class of 2027 eligibility section separately states that an applicant must have completed at least one year of coursework toward an associate or bachelor s degree . Applicants should therefore ensure they satisfy the formal eligibility requirement, rather than interpreting the transcript-upload requirement as reducing it to one semester. One Letter of Recommendation Only one recommendation letter is required. The recommender should be someone who genuinely knows the applicant and can provide meaningful evidence about their strengths, achievements and character. Potential recommenders may include: Teachers. Professors. Coaches. Mentors. Supervisors. Club leaders. Other appropriate professional or academic contacts. A family member or personal friend should not be used as the recommender. The letter should ideally provide evidence of the applicant s character, creativity, consistency, service and impact in the communities in which they participate. The official FAQ confirms that applicants need one recommendation and only one will be accepted . Three Original Application Components For 2027, applicants are asked to prepare three original works intended to help reviewers understand them beyond their transcript and resume. These are: A Personal Statement of no more than 600 words. A Mission Alignment Essay of no more than 300 words. A Multimedia Essay in a format other than a conventional written essay. Together, these submissions are intended to provide insight into three broad dimensions: Professional and academic interests. Personal character, values and passions. Commitment to service, community and creating opportunities for others. Personal Statement: Maximum 600 Words The personal statement allows applicants to communicate who they are beyond their academic record. Applicants are encouraged to discuss the passions, values, experiences, goals and personal qualities that have shaped them and their ambitions. The objective is not simply to repeat a resume. A strong personal statement should help reviewers understand: What motivates you. What experiences have shaped you. What matters to you. What kind of person you are. Where you want your career to go. What you would contribute to the Brooke Owens community. The program specifically encourages applicants to be authentic, specific and reflective. Mission Alignment Essay: Maximum 300 Words The 2027 application also includes a Mission Alignment Essay , limited to 300 words. This component asks candidates to reflect on the Brooke Owens Fellowship s mission of expanding aerospace opportunities for women and gender minorities. Applicants should explain why this mission matters to them and how they hope to contribute to it throughout their careers. Potential themes include: Creating more inclusive professional environments. Mentoring future students. Expanding access to aerospace opportunities. Addressing structural barriers. Using leadership positions to support others. Helping future professionals enter and thrive in aerospace. The Fellowship encourages applicants to connect their answers with their lived experiences and consider how they could use future leadership or influence to make aerospace more welcoming and equitable. Multimedia Essay: Show Creativity Beyond a Written Application The Multimedia Essay is deliberately different from a conventional university application essay. Applicants must not submit another traditional written essay. Instead, they should communicate their ideas through a creative digital format. Past formats have included: Short videos. Original songs. Spoken-word pieces. Animations. Graphic designs. Podcasts. Comic strips. Other creative digital formats. Multimedia Submission Requirements The submission must: Be fully digital. Require no physical mailing. Be accessible through commonly available software. Not require passwords or obscure software. Be reviewable or playable in five minutes or less. Remain below 250 MB in file size. 2027 Multimedia Essay Prompts Applicants can respond creatively to one of the prompts listed for the Class of 2027. The themes focus on: A situation where the applicant had to be resourceful and work within constraints. An experience serving a community and the resulting impact. A project or activity in which the applicant became deeply engaged and demonstrated enthusiasm or creativity. A situation where the applicant challenged an established system, norm or assumption. How intentional decision-making has influenced the applicant s actions and outcomes. These prompts are designed to reveal qualities such as: Resourcefulness. Creativity. Values. Service. Teamwork. Enthusiasm. Courage. Independent thinking. Leadership. Self-awareness. Intentionality. Important File Submission Rules Applicants should carefully test every file before submitting the application. The Fellowship specifically warns that an application cannot be edited after submission . Before submitting: Test video links. Confirm that file-sharing permissions work. Make sure reviewers will not encounter access restrictions. Check that all files open correctly. Verify multimedia runtime. Keep files below the required 250 MB limit. Proofread written documents. Confirm that the correct versions have been uploaded. The application page also recommends including the relevant prompt directly with each original work so reviewers can easily identify the question being addressed. One detail worth noting is that the current page explicitly identifies three original works , including the 300-word Mission Alignment Essay, while its later file-submission checklist lists the resume, transcript, recommendation letter, personal statement and multimedia essay without repeating the mission essay. Applicants should follow the live application portal carefully and prepare the Mission Alignment Essay because it is expressly listed as a required original work earlier on the official 2027 application page. Are International Students Eligible? Yes. U.S. citizenship is not required. The official FAQ states that students of all nationalities are welcome to apply , while the official application portal describes the fellowship as bringing together undergraduate students from around the world. There is, however, an important practical qualification for international applicants. Some aerospace opportunities may be subject to U.S. export-control or International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) restrictions. These requirements can limit eligibility for particular jobs or host-company roles based on citizenship or immigration status. The Fellowship states that it works with Fellows individually to identify opportunities that fit their circumstances. International students should therefore not interpret ITAR restrictions as a general ban on applying . They are eligible for the Fellowship itself, although the range of specific industry placements available to them may differ. Virtual Information Sessions for the Class of 2027 The Fellowship is also hosting virtual information sessions for prospective applicants. The published Class of 2027 sessions, with times given in EDT, are: September 13, 2026 at 2:00 PM EDT September 19, 2026 at 12:00 PM EDT , featuring international students September 28, 2026 at 10:00 PM EDT The session specifically featuring international students may be particularly useful for applicants with questions about citizenship requirements, aerospace placements and participation from outside the United States. Ask a Brookie Application Support Applicants who want advice from someone who has previously completed the fellowship process can use the program s Ask a Brookie resource. Past Fellows can provide guidance about matters such as: Their fellowship experience. How they approached application essays. Internship preparation. Joining the Fellowship community. General application strategy. For formal questions concerning eligibility, applicants are advised to use the Fellowship s official eligibility information or contact its administration rather than relying solely on peer advice. How Applicants Are Selected The program emphasizes holistic assessment rather than relying on one numerical indicator. According to its FAQ, applications are reviewed by aerospace professionals and Brooke Owens alumni. The program considers the overall application, including personal and creative materials, recommendations and alignment with the Fellowship s values. There is no published minimum GPA cutoff and no single factor automatically determines selection. This makes it important for applicants to submit a coherent application where the different components reinforce one another. For example: Your resume shows what you have done. Your transcript gives academic context. Your recommendation provides an outside perspective. Your personal statement shows who you are. Your Mission Alignment Essay explains how your values connect with the program. Your multimedia project demonstrates creativity, character and perspective. What Makes a Strong Application? While there is no guaranteed formula, applicants should pay particular attention to the qualities the Fellowship repeatedly emphasizes. Be Authentic Do not attempt to construct what you imagine a stereotypical aerospace candidate should look like. The application is specifically designed to identify talent that may not always be recognized through conventional recruitment methods. Demonstrate Service Community involvement is an important theme throughout the application. Show what you have actually done for other people, organizations or communities. Demonstrate Aerospace Interest You do not need to study aerospace engineering, but your application should make it credible that aerospace is genuinely part of your intended career direction. Show Creativity This matters particularly in the multimedia submission. Use a format that strengthens your message rather than selecting something elaborate simply because it appears impressive. Explain Your Values The program wants to understand what motivates your decisions and how your values affect the way you work with others. Proofread Everything A creative application can still be weakened by avoidable mistakes, inaccessible links or unclear writing. Start Early The application includes several components requiring substantial reflection, plus a recommendation from another person. Waiting until the final day substantially increases the risk of an incomplete or technically flawed application. Application Timeline September 1, 2026 Applications officially opened at 12:00 AM EDT . September 13, 2026 First Class of 2027 virtual information session at 2:00 PM EDT. September 19, 2026 International-student-focused virtual information session at 12:00 PM EDT. September 28, 2026 Final listed virtual information session at 10:00 PM EDT. October 4, 2026 Application deadline at 11:59 PM EDT. The Fellowship s FAQ indicates that semifinalists are typically contacted within several weeks after applications close, with finalists subsequently selected through interviews and the complete class announced during the winter. How to Apply for the Brooke Owens Fellowship Class of 2027 Prospective applicants should: Confirm that they meet the Class of 2027 eligibility requirements. Review the entire official application guide. Create an account in the application portal. Prepare an updated resume or CV. Obtain an appropriate academic transcript. Select one recommender and provide sufficient time for the recommendation. Draft the Personal Statement within the 600-word limit. Prepare the Mission Alignment Essay within the 300-word limit. Select one multimedia prompt. Create an original non-prose multimedia submission. Confirm that the multimedia content is reviewable in five minutes or less. Keep the relevant digital file under 250 MB. Check links, permissions and file accessibility. Review the entire application carefully. Submit before October 4, 2026 at 11:59 PM EDT . Do not wait until the final minutes because applications cannot be corrected after submission. Apply for the Brooke Owens Fellowship Class of 2027 Why Students Interested in Aerospace Should Consider Applying The Brooke Owens Fellowship offers something difficult to reproduce through an ordinary internship application: a combination of industry experience, structured mentorship, professional development and access to a continuing aerospace community. The program s record now includes hundreds of Fellows, more than one hundred host organizations and more than one hundred mentors. Its alumni network extends across aerospace research, engineering, operations, policy, technology, entrepreneurship and other areas. For students who are serious about aerospace but have not traditionally seen themselves represented in the industry, the program is designed to create both access and a support structure for long-term career development. Conclusion Applications for the Brooke Owens Fellowship Class of 2027 provide undergraduate women and gender-minority students with an opportunity to build professional experience, receive mentorship from experienced aerospace professionals, participate in professional development and join an established community of emerging aerospace leaders. The program is intentionally multidisciplinary. Applicants do not need to major in aerospace engineering, there is no published minimum GPA, and U.S. citizenship is not required. What matters is that applicants meet the undergraduate and age requirements, identify within the gender groups the program serves, and demonstrate genuine interest in pursuing an aerospace career. The application is more extensive than a conventional internship form. Candidates need to prepare a resume or CV, academic transcript, one recommendation letter, a Personal Statement, a Mission Alignment Essay and a creative Multimedia Essay. Applicants should therefore start preparing their materials early. Applications close October 4, 2026 at 11:59 PM EDT. Official Application Page For more global opportunities, click HERE . title: 2030STEM Fellowship 2026: Apply for a US$10,000 Career Development Award for STEM Researchers and Professionals
summary: Applications are open for the 2030STEM Fellowship 2026 , a career-development opportunity designed to support early- to mid-career researchers and professionals working across science, technology, engineering, mathematics, and related STEM fields. For the 2026 cycle, 2030STEM is seeking five STEM professionals to serve as Fellows , with each selected Fellow receiving a US$10,000 award that can be used to advance their professional career. The fellowship is intended to provide flexible career-development support while recognizing STEM professionals who demonstrate leadership, community building, knowledge translation, and the potential to contribute to meaningful change within the STEM ecosystem. The funding can support a range of professional-development needs, including conference participation, research-related expenses, childcare, and other costs connected with career advancement. Rather than prescribing one single route to professional development, the program acknowledges that STEM professionals may face different financial, institutional, professional, and personal barriers at different stages of their careers. 2030STEM Fellowship 2026 at a Glance Detail Information Opportunity 2030STEM Fellowship Application 2026 Organizer 2030STEM Number of Fellows 5 Award US$10,000 per selected Fellow Target Group Early- to mid-career STEM researchers and professionals Fields STEM disciplines and professional areas Funding Purpose Career development Examples of Eligible Uses Conference travel, research expenses, childcare and other career-development needs Application Method Online application References Required Names and email addresses of three references CV/Resume Required Selection Emphasis Community building, knowledge translation and innovative STEM leadership Application Deadline Not stated on the current 2026 application form Application Status The online application form was live when reviewed on September 4, 2026 The current application form does not display a formal closing date. Applicants should therefore avoid assuming that applications will remain open indefinitely and should consider submitting as early as possible after confirming that they meet the intended applicant profile. What Is the 2030STEM Fellowship? 2030STEM describes the initiative as a catalytic resource intended to advance the careers of STEM researchers and professionals. The central idea behind the fellowship is that scientific and technological progress depends not only on institutions, laboratories and funding mechanisms but also on the people conducting research, communicating scientific knowledge, building professional communities and providing leadership. The program therefore seeks professionals who can advance their own careers while also contributing to improvements in the broader culture and structure of STEM. According to the 2026 application, successful candidates are expected to have demonstrated a strong history in three important areas: Building community. Translating knowledge. Demonstrating innovative leadership in STEM. These elements indicate that applicants should present themselves not simply as technically qualified scientists or professionals but as individuals whose work has influenced colleagues, communities, institutions, research environments or wider audiences. About 2030STEM 2030STEM is an initiative working toward systemic change within science, technology, engineering and mathematics. Its broader work focuses on areas including: Full inclusion in STEM. Leadership development. Institutional change. Access to capital. Professional advancement. Community development. Improved pathways for historically underrepresented STEM professionals. 2030STEM states that its work takes a systems-level approach to strengthening professional self-efficacy, STEM and cultural identities, self-advocacy, leadership pathways and institutional structures. The organization particularly emphasizes increasing representation and leadership opportunities for Black, Latino/a/x, Indigenous and other people of color throughout STEM disciplines and sectors. Its broader strategy includes improving access to professional networks, capital, leadership opportunities and institutional support. Why the 2030STEM Fellowship Matters Career advancement in STEM can require resources that traditional research grants, university funding or employer budgets do not always cover. Researchers and professionals may need financial support to: Attend important scientific conferences. Conduct or advance research. Access professional-development opportunities. Build collaborations. Travel to laboratories, institutions or meetings. Obtain equipment or other resources connected with professional advancement. Manage childcare responsibilities while participating in professional activities. Strengthen their professional networks. Explore new research directions. Position themselves for future leadership opportunities. The 2026 fellowship addresses this challenge by providing selected professionals with US$10,000 toward their career development. Importantly, the application itself specifically identifies conference travel, research expenses and childcare as examples of potential career-development needs. How Much Funding Is Available? Each selected 2030STEM Fellow will receive: US$10,000 toward career advancement. The 2026 call states that five STEM professionals are being sought for the fellowship. This represents a potential combined allocation of US$50,000 across the five selected Fellows, although applicants should understand that the official application describes the award individually as US$10,000 for each Fellow. What Can the US$10,000 Be Used For? The fellowship is designed around career development rather than one narrowly prescribed research project. The application specifically provides examples including: Conference Travel Funding could help a Fellow participate in professional or scientific conferences that are important for: Presenting research. Networking with collaborators. Learning about emerging developments. Meeting prospective mentors. Connecting with employers or research institutions. Building visibility within a specialist field. Research Expenses The award may also contribute to expenses associated with advancing the Fellow s research or professional work. The application does not provide an exhaustive list of eligible research costs, so applicants should explain clearly how their proposed expense will contribute to their professional advancement. Childcare One particularly notable aspect of the fellowship is the explicit recognition of childcare as a potential career-development expense. Professional travel, conferences, fieldwork and other career activities can create additional care responsibilities. By explicitly mentioning childcare, the fellowship recognizes that career barriers are not limited to laboratory or academic costs. Other Career-Development Needs The application uses the phrase “including but not limited to,” indicating that the stated examples are not necessarily the only possible uses. Applicants should therefore identify the career-development expenditure that is most relevant to their circumstances and clearly explain how the US$10,000 would produce a meaningful professional outcome. What Type of Applicants Is 2030STEM Looking For? The 2026 call specifically describes its target group as early- to mid-career STEM researchers and professionals . The strongest candidates are expected to demonstrate a history of: Building meaningful professional or scientific communities. Communicating or translating knowledge. Exercising innovative leadership. Advancing science or STEM practice. Supporting broader improvements within STEM environments. Applicants should therefore think beyond conventional achievements such as publications, degrees or job titles. The fellowship questions suggest that reviewers are interested in understanding: Where the applicant wants their career to go. What motivates their STEM career. How the applicant contributes to other people or communities. How they communicate knowledge. What kind of leadership they demonstrate. How funding would change or accelerate their career trajectory. 2030STEM s Approach to STEM Inclusion The broader mission of 2030STEM is closely connected with improving representation and opportunity across the STEM ecosystem. The organization argues that STEM institutions benefit when professionals from different backgrounds participate fully in scientific research, decision-making and leadership. Its stated work places substantial emphasis on improving opportunities for Black, Latino/a/x, Indigenous and other people of color in STEM, including by addressing structural barriers that can affect recruitment, retention, promotion, leadership and access to financial resources. However, applicants should distinguish the organization s broader mission from the formal requirements displayed on the current 2026 application form . The live 2026 form does not present a race or ethnicity field as an explicit eligibility condition. Application Requirements The 2030STEM Fellowship application requests a combination of personal details, professional information, career reflections and supporting documentation. Applicants should be prepared to provide the following. 1. Full Name Applicants must provide their first and last name. Use the same professional name that appears on your CV, publications, institutional profile and other professional records wherever possible. 2. Email Address A valid email address is required. Applicants should preferably use an email account that they monitor regularly because fellowship communications and potential follow-up regarding the selection process may be sent to this address. 3. Phone Number Applicants are required to provide a valid telephone number. 4. Highest Level of Education The application asks applicants to identify their highest completed level of education. The current 2026 form does not, within the publicly accessible text reviewed, state a specific minimum degree requirement. Applicants should therefore report their educational background accurately rather than assuming that the qualification requirements from a previous fellowship cycle automatically apply to the 2026 call. 5. Current Field or Area of Expertise Applicants must state their current field or professional area of expertise. This is an important part of establishing the applicant s connection to STEM. Applicants should use a specific description where possible. Instead of simply writing “science,” for example, an applicant may identify areas such as: Molecular biology. Environmental science. Artificial intelligence. Engineering. Chemistry. Astronomy. Biomedical research. Climate science. Data science. Mathematics. Physics. Public health research. Computer science. Scientific communication. Engineering education. The exact field should reflect the applicant s genuine professional background. 6. Current Affiliation Applicants must provide their present institutional or professional affiliation. This could potentially include a university, research institution, government entity, company, laboratory, nonprofit organization or other professional organization, depending on the applicant s circumstances. Five-Year Career Vision One of the application questions asks applicants to explain where they see themselves professionally over the next five years. Applicants are also asked to discuss: The type of science they expect to be doing. The people or types of professionals with whom they hope to collaborate. This question gives applicants an opportunity to demonstrate that they have a meaningful career direction. A strong response should connect: Current position → professional development need → fellowship support → five-year objective. Applicants should avoid writing only about a desired job title. Instead, they can describe the scientific or professional impact they want to create. Explain the Pivotal Moment Behind Your STEM Career Applicants are asked to: Share a pivotal moment or experience that significantly influenced their decision to pursue their current STEM career path. This question is more personal than a conventional CV-based application question. The objective appears to be understanding the applicant s motivation, trajectory and relationship with their chosen STEM field. Applicants may consider discussing an experience such as: Exposure to an important scientific problem. A research experience. A mentor who influenced their career. A community challenge that inspired their work. An academic breakthrough. An internship or professional experience. A personal experience that led to a scientific question. A problem the applicant became determined to solve. The response should remain authentic and directly connected to the applicant s career development. Demonstrate Community Building, Knowledge Translation and Leadership This is one of the most important components of the application. Applicants must explain how they or their work have contributed to: Building community. Translating knowledge. Innovative leadership in STEM. Applicants should support their answer with concrete examples. Potential evidence may include: Creating research networks. Mentoring students or younger researchers. Leading professional groups. Developing interdisciplinary collaborations. Communicating scientific research to non-specialist audiences. Working with communities affected by scientific or technological issues. Translating research findings into policy or practice. Developing new scientific initiatives. Creating inclusive professional environments. Leading institutional changes. Developing innovative research methods or approaches. Simply describing yourself as a leader will generally be less persuasive than demonstrating what you led, who benefited and what changed. Explain How You Would Use the US$10,000 Applicants are specifically asked: If selected, how will you use the funds toward advancing your career? This response should be clear, realistic and connected with professional development. A strong answer could explain: What the funding would purchase or support. Why that particular expenditure is necessary. Why existing institutional resources cannot fully cover it, where applicable. What professional outcome the expenditure would produce. How that outcome connects with the applicant s longer-term STEM career. Applicants should avoid treating the US$10,000 simply as a financial prize. The application frames the funding specifically around career advancement . Three Professional References Are Required Applicants must provide the name and email address of three references . Importantly, the application states that references will only be contacted if the applicant progresses to the second round . Applicants should therefore select references carefully. Suitable references will generally be people who can credibly discuss the applicant s: STEM expertise. Research or professional accomplishments. Leadership. Community contributions. Collaboration. Communication skills. Professional potential. Applicants should obtain permission from references before listing their contact information and make sure the email addresses entered in the application are accurate. Resume or CV Requirement Applicants are also asked to upload a resume or curriculum vitae . The CV should reinforce the story presented throughout the application. Relevant sections could include: Education. Current position. Research experience. Professional experience. Publications. Presentations. Fellowships. Awards. Grants. Professional leadership. Community engagement. Science communication. Mentoring. Professional societies. Relevant projects. Applicants should ensure that dates, affiliations and accomplishments mentioned in their written responses are consistent with the information appearing on their CV. Additional Information Section The application concludes with an optional question asking whether there is anything else the selection team should know about the applicant . Applicants should use this space strategically. Rather than repeating information already stated elsewhere, it may be useful for providing context that is genuinely relevant to the application but has not been captured by the previous questions. How Applicants Can Strengthen Their Application The current application does not publish a numerical evaluation rubric. The following points should therefore be treated as practical application guidance rather than official scoring criteria. Demonstrate Impact, Not Only Achievement Instead of simply listing accomplishments, explain the effect of those accomplishments. For example: Who benefited? What problem was addressed? What changed? What was created? What did the applicant personally contribute? Connect Your Career Vision With the Funding The five-year career question and the funding-use question should support one another. If an applicant wants to become a leader in a particular research area, the proposed use of funding should logically move them toward that objective. Provide Evidence of Community Building Since community building is specifically mentioned by 2030STEM, applicants should identify concrete examples of how they have supported colleagues, students, professional communities or other stakeholders. Explain Knowledge Translation Knowledge translation can involve turning specialist research into information that can be understood or applied by: Policymakers. Communities. Students. Industry. Healthcare professionals. Educators. Other researchers. The general public. Applicants should demonstrate actual communication or application rather than merely saying that science communication is important. Show Innovative Leadership Leadership does not necessarily require holding a senior management position. Applicants may demonstrate leadership by initiating projects, solving problems, creating collaborations, mentoring others, changing institutional practices or introducing new scientific approaches. Previous 2030STEM Fellowship Context 2030STEM previously operated the 2030STEM × Burroughs Wellcome Fund Fellowship . The 2025 program also focused on advancing early- to mid-career STEM professionals and provided US$10,000 to Fellows. The earlier fellowship included a two-year professional-development structure involving cohort meetings, career-development workshops and access to the 2030STEM Champions network. The current 2026 application form does not display those restrictions . Instead, it asks applicants to provide their highest education level, STEM field and current affiliation. Anyone uncertain about eligibility should rely on the current application and any additional instructions issued directly by 2030STEM. Because the organization is selecting only five Fellows, interested candidates should prepare and submit their applications promptly rather than waiting for an unconfirmed closing date. Applicants should also recheck the application page before submitting in case a deadline or additional instructions are subsequently added. How to Apply for the 2030STEM Fellowship 2026 Applicants can follow these steps: Review the fellowship description carefully. Prepare your current resume or CV. Confirm your highest educational qualification. Clearly identify your current STEM field or area of expertise. Provide your current professional or institutional affiliation. Develop a clear five-year career vision. Identify a pivotal experience that influenced your STEM career. Prepare examples demonstrating community building. Explain how you translate scientific or technical knowledge. Demonstrate innovative leadership. Develop a specific plan for using the US$10,000 award. Select three appropriate professional references. Obtain their correct names and email addresses. Complete all required sections of the online form. Upload your resume or CV. Review the application carefully. Submit the application while the form remains open. Application and reference link: Apply for the 2030STEM Fellowship 2026 The shortened reference link directs applicants to the official 2030STEM Fellowship Application 2026 hosted on Jotform. Why STEM Professionals Should Consider Applying The 2030STEM Fellowship differs from many conventional research opportunities because its focus is the professional themselves and their career advancement , rather than solely funding a tightly defined research proposal. The US$10,000 support can potentially help selected Fellows overcome practical barriers that prevent them from pursuing important professional opportunities. For an early- or mid-career STEM professional, access to funding at the right stage could help support research, participation in an important conference, collaboration-building or another strategic professional-development activity. At the same time, the application clearly signals that 2030STEM is interested in people who contribute beyond their individual technical work. Applicants who can demonstrate a combination of scientific capability, professional ambition, community engagement, communication and innovative leadership may be particularly aligned with the program s stated objectives. Application Checklist Before submitting, applicants should make sure they have: Full name. Active email address. Valid telephone number. Highest level of education. Current field or area of expertise. Current professional affiliation. A clear five-year career vision. Information about the type of science or STEM work they plan to pursue. Potential collaborators or collaboration goals. A meaningful pivotal STEM career experience. Examples of community building. Examples of knowledge translation. Examples of innovative leadership. A clear plan for using the US$10,000. Names of three references. Email addresses of all three references. Updated resume or CV. Conclusion The 2030STEM Fellowship 2026 provides an important career-development opportunity for early- to mid-career researchers and professionals seeking resources to advance their work and expand their impact within STEM. 2030STEM is selecting five Fellows , with each successful applicant receiving US$10,000 toward career advancement . Potential uses identified in the application include conference travel, research expenses, childcare and other career-development needs. title: HWCC Conference Travel Grants 2027: Apply for Free Registration or Up to US$1,000 to Attend the Bangkok Conference
summary: Applications are open for a limited number of travel grants supporting participation in the 2nd International Conference on Human-Wildlife Conflict and Coexistence, which will take place from March 2–4, 2027, in Bangkok, Thailand. Successful applicants may receive either a conference registration fee waiver or financial assistance of US$500 or US$1,000 toward travel costs. Applicants can request only one of these three support options. The application window runs from September 1 to October 31, 2026. All applications must be submitted in English through the official online form by 23:59 GMT on October 31, 2026 . Applicants are expected to receive the outcome of their applications by November 15, 2026. The official travel-grant page confirms the deadline, support options and priority criteria . Travel Grant Opportunity at a Glance Detail Information Opportunity name Travel Support for the 2nd International Conference on Human-Wildlife Conflict and Coexistence Conference dates March 2–4, 2027 Location Bangkok, Thailand Venue Avani+ Riverside Bangkok Hotel Application opening date September 1, 2026 Application deadline October 31, 2026, at 23:59 GMT Notification date By November 15, 2026 Application language English Available support Registration waiver or reimbursement, US$500 toward travel, or US$1,000 toward travel Number of options allowed Applicants may request only one support option Conference registration required before applying No Application method Online Google application form Host IUCN SSC Human-Wildlife Conflict Coexistence Specialist Group About the 2nd International Conference on Human-Wildlife Conflict and Coexistence The 2nd International Conference on Human-Wildlife Conflict and Coexistence will bring together people working across conservation, research, policy, development, agriculture, technology and community-based practice. Human-wildlife conflict can occur when interactions between people and wildlife create actual or perceived negative consequences for human livelihoods, safety, well-being, conservation objectives or animal welfare. Addressing these challenges requires more than biological research. It frequently involves community participation, governance, economic incentives, land-use planning, communication, behavioral science, conflict resolution and public policy. The conference is being organized by the IUCN Species Survival Commission’s Human-Wildlife Conflict and Coexistence Specialist Group. It will build on the first international conference, held in Oxford in 2023, which brought together nearly 600 participants from 70 countries and all continents. The second conference will be held over three days in Bangkok from March 2–4, 2027. It is expected to convene Indigenous and local community leaders, conservation practitioners, researchers, government representatives, grant-makers, policymakers and professionals from other relevant sectors. The official conference overview explains its international, cross-sectoral focus . Main Objectives of the Conference The conference aims to improve international cooperation and learning on human-wildlife conflict and coexistence. Its stated objectives include: Promoting a shared understanding of human-wildlife conflict and coexistence through new perspectives, scientific knowledge, practical insights and technological advances. Supporting the development of frameworks and approaches that improve research, management and mitigation. Encouraging approaches that can influence national and international policies concerning human-wildlife conflict. Facilitating dialogue and learning between different professional sectors and academic disciplines. Examining emerging dimensions of human-wildlife conflict and coexistence. Supporting local, national and international collaboration between practitioners, policymakers, researchers, communities and other stakeholders. Advancing interdisciplinary approaches that consider the ecological, social, economic, cultural, political and behavioral dimensions of human-wildlife interactions. The event is intended to provide a platform for practical discussion, knowledge exchange, professional networking and the development of new collaborations. What Support Is Available? Applicants must select only one of the following three options in the application form. Option 1: Free Conference Registration Successful applicants under this option will have their conference registration fee waived. The organizers will send successful recipients a registration form so that they can register and confirm their place at the conference. If a successful applicant has already registered and paid for a conference ticket, the organizers state that the ticket cost will be reimbursed. This option may be useful for applicants who can arrange their own transportation and accommodation but cannot afford the conference registration fee. Option 2: US$500 Toward Travel Costs Applicants may request US$500 toward the costs of travelling to Bangkok. The official page states that successful recipients will receive the amount in cash and in person at the conference on March 3, 2027. The webpage does not state that the organizers will purchase airline tickets, reserve accommodation or provide the US$500 before the conference. Applicants should therefore plan on arranging and initially financing their travel unless their award letter expressly states otherwise. Option 3: US$1,000 Toward Travel Costs Applicants from eligible locations may request US$1,000 toward travel expenses. As with the US$500 option, the amount will be provided in cash and in person at the conference in Bangkok on March 3, 2027. The award letter issued to each successful applicant will confirm the payment arrangement. The US$1,000 option is not available to applicants based in: Bangladesh Bhutan Brunei Cambodia China India Indonesia Laos Malaysia Maldives Myanmar Nepal Philippines Singapore Sri Lanka Taiwan Thailand Vietnam Applicants from these locations may still select the free conference registration option or the US$500 travel-support option, provided they otherwise satisfy the requirements. Important Funding Limitation The travel-grant programme is not described as full sponsorship. Applicants should understand the following points: Only a limited number of awards are available. Submitting an application does not guarantee funding. Applicants may request only one support option. A US$500 or US$1,000 travel award is not described as including free conference registration. A registration waiver is not described as including airfare, accommodation or other travel expenses. The travel money is scheduled to be distributed in person on March 3, 2027. The webpage does not promise advance payment or direct flight booking. The webpage does not specify whether visa costs, accommodation, insurance or local transportation qualify as travel expenses. The final award letter will confirm the arrangement offered to each recipient. Applicants should prepare a realistic financial plan covering any costs not included in their selected support option. A Critical Cash-Flow Consideration The timing of the travel-grant payment is particularly important. The main conference starts on March 2, 2027, while the US$500 or US$1,000 award is scheduled to be paid in person on March 3, 2027. This means recipients may need to purchase their tickets, obtain a visa, arrange insurance, book accommodation and reach Bangkok before receiving the money. Applicants should not assume that selection will remove the need for advance funds. Before accepting an award, recipients should confirm: Whether they must purchase their own airline ticket. Whether any payment can be made before departure. Whether the award may be used for accommodation. Whether proof of expenditure will be required. Whether conference registration must be purchased separately. Whether payment will be made in U.S. dollars or an equivalent local currency. Whether identification or a signed receipt will be required to collect the cash. What happens if the recipient experiences a visa refusal or travel disruption. Unless the award letter states otherwise, applicants should treat the funding as a contribution toward attendance rather than complete coverage of every cost. Who Receives Priority? The official page does not state that applicants must meet every priority criterion. It says priority will be given to applicants who meet any of the following: Residents of countries not classified as high-income under the World Bank country classification. Students from any country. Applicants who submitted an abstract for a talk, poster or session. Individuals included in a conference session submitted by another person. These are priority factors rather than clearly stated absolute eligibility restrictions. Therefore, the published information does not explicitly exclude: Non-students. Applicants from high-income countries. Applicants who did not submit an abstract. Applicants who are not presenting at the conference. People working outside universities. Independent practitioners and consultants. Private-sector professionals. Government employees. Members of nonprofit or intergovernmental organizations. However, applicants who do not meet any priority criterion may face stronger competition because the available funding is limited. Do Applicants Need to Register for the Conference First? No. Applicants do not need to register for the conference before submitting a travel-support application. This is important because one of the available options is a registration fee waiver. Applicants seeking this option do not need to pay the registration fee merely to qualify for consideration. Those who have already purchased a ticket may still apply. If they are selected for the registration-support option, the organizers state that the ticket will be reimbursed. Applicants should keep their: Registration confirmation. Payment receipt. Invoice. Card or bank transaction record. Any correspondence with the conference organizer. These records may be needed to arrange reimbursement. Status of the Call for Contributions The conference’s separate call for abstracts and session contributions closed on August 31, 2026. The travel-grant application opened on September 1, 2026. Consequently, applicants who submitted an abstract, poster, talk or session proposal before the contributions deadline may receive priority during travel-grant consideration. Someone who did not submit a contribution may still apply for travel assistance because submitting an abstract is not stated as a mandatory requirement. However, the person cannot now rely on that particular priority factor unless the organizers reopen the contributions process. The conference accepted proposals across a broad range of subjects, including: Human, cultural and behavioral dimensions of coexistence. Landscape-scale, climate and ecological issues. Development, livelihoods, food security, poverty and well-being. Communications and media. Technology, artificial intelligence and scientific innovation. Compensation, insurance, incentives and other financial instruments. Practical conflict resolution and peacebuilding. Policy and governance. Connections between science and policy. Lived experience and traditional knowledge. One Health approaches. Animal behavior, ethics and animal welfare. The contribution formats included symposia, panels, reverse panels, interactive sessions, workshops, film screenings, individual presentations, speed talks and posters. The official contribution page confirms that submissions are now closed . Application Form Requirements The official application form is relatively short. It currently requests the following information: Personal and contact information Applicants must provide: First and last name. Email address. Main country of residence. Employment and affiliation Applicants must identify the type of organization with which they work. The form provides the following options: Government. Private sector. NGO or nonprofit organization. Intergovernmental organization. Academia or research institution. Independent or consultancy. Other. Applicants must also state their organization or professional affiliation. Student status The application asks whether the applicant is currently a student. Students from any country are one of the groups given priority, but the form also allows non-students to apply. Conference contribution status Applicants must state whether they submitted an abstract to the conference. The form also asks whether they have been included as a panelist or speaker in a proposal submitted by another person. Available responses are: Yes. No. I do not know. Funding justification statement Applicants must respond to the following substantive question in no more than 150 words: Explain how attending the conference will further your work in human-wildlife conflict and coexistence and why you need financial support to attend. This is the main written justification on the current form. Applicants should use the limited word count carefully. Requested grant option Applicants must choose one of the following: Free conference registration. US$500 toward travel costs. US$1,000 toward travel costs, where geographically available. The current form does not display a requirement to upload a curriculum vitae, passport, recommendation letter, academic transcript, detailed budget or copy of an abstract. Applicants should nevertheless recheck the live form before submission in case the organizers make changes. How to Write a Strong 150-Word Funding Statement The 150-word response should address both parts of the question: How attending will advance the applicant’s work. Why the applicant cannot attend without financial assistance. A practical structure could be: Opening: Professional or community context Briefly introduce your work and the human-wildlife conflict issue you address. For example, explain whether you work in conservation, research, agriculture, public policy, local government, community development, animal welfare, livelihoods or another related area. Current challenge Identify the specific problem, knowledge gap or implementation challenge affecting your work. Avoid relying only on broad statements such as “human-wildlife conflict is important.” Describe the particular problem your community, institution or project is facing. Value of conference participation Explain how the conference will help you: Learn a specific approach. Connect with relevant specialists. improve an existing intervention. Strengthen policy development. Develop a collaboration. Share community knowledge. Apply research findings. Bring practical lessons back to your institution or community. Financial need State clearly why assistance is necessary. Where relevant, mention limited institutional funding, student status, unfavorable exchange rates, long-distance travel costs or lack of access to professional-development funding. Applicants should remain factual and avoid making unsupported claims. Suggested 150-Word Allocation Applicants may use the following approximate structure: 30–40 words: Your role and the human-wildlife issue you address. 35–45 words: The practical problem or knowledge gap affecting your work. 40–50 words: How conference learning and connections will improve your work. 20–30 words: Why financial support is necessary. 10–20 words: The outcome you intend to deliver after returning. This is application guidance rather than an official scoring formula. How Applications Are Expected to Be Reviewed The organizers have not published a numerical scoring system, detailed assessment rubric or weighting for each criterion. The official information only confirms that: Funding is limited. Applications will be assessed against available resources. Priority will be given to the specified applicant groups. Selection is not guaranteed. Applicants should therefore avoid claims that meeting one priority criterion guarantees an award. A strong application should demonstrate: A clear connection to human-wildlife conflict and coexistence. A practical reason for attending the conference. A realistic benefit to the applicant’s work, organization or community. Genuine financial need. A credible plan to apply or share knowledge gained from the conference. Accurate information about student, residence and contribution status. Travel-Grant Application Timeline August 31, 2026 The separate call for abstracts and session contributions closed. September 1, 2026 Travel-grant applications opened. September 15, 2026 The conference’s early-bird registration deadline was extended to this date. Applicants do not need to register before applying for travel support. October 31, 2026 Travel-grant applications close at 23:59 GMT . November 15, 2026 All applicants are expected to be notified of the result by this date. March 1, 2027 Optional pre-conference short courses are scheduled. These courses are separately ticketed and are not automatically included in the main registration fee. March 2–4, 2027 The main conference takes place in Bangkok. March 3, 2027 Successful US$500 and US$1,000 recipients are scheduled to receive their awards in cash and in person. The separately ticketed conference dinner is also scheduled for this date. Conference Venue The conference will be held at: Avani+ Riverside Bangkok Hotel 257 Charoen Nakhon Road Samre, Thon Buri Bangkok 10600 Thailand The hotel is a riverside venue overlooking the Chao Phraya River. It can be reached from both Suvarnabhumi Airport and Don Mueang Airport using taxis or ride-hailing services. Delegates arriving at Suvarnabhumi Airport may also use the Airport Rail Link, connect to the BTS Skytrain and travel to Saphan Taksin Station before using the hotel’s shuttle boat. Complete venue and transportation information is available on the official conference website . What Conference Registration Includes According to the registration page, the main conference registration fee includes: Access to sessions in the main conference programme. Tea, coffee and snacks twice each day. Lunch on all three conference days. Admission to the conference reception. The following are optional or separately ticketed: Conference dinner. Pre-conference short courses. Other separately advertised activities. Registration does not automatically cover international travel, accommodation, visas, insurance or other personal expenses. The official registration page explains what the ticket includes . Visa, Passport and Insurance Responsibilities International participants are responsible for checking the entry requirements that apply to their nationality and travel documents. Delegates should plan for: A passport valid for the required period. A Thai visa or electronic visa where applicable. Thailand’s entry and arrival requirements. Travel and health insurance. Cancellation insurance where appropriate. Vaccination or health documentation if required. Sufficient funds for accommodation and daily expenses. Contingency costs caused by delays or cancellations. Thailand requires international visitors to complete the Thailand Digital Arrival Card before arrival. Entry rules can change, so selected applicants should verify requirements through official Thai government sources before booking travel. The conference terms state that the organizer may issue visa-support letters only after registration and payment have been completed. A support letter does not guarantee visa approval. Applicants should review the conference’s current visa guidance . How to Apply Follow these steps: Read the official travel-grant information . Decide which single support option best matches your financial situation. Open the official travel-grant application form . Enter your name, email address and main country of residence. Select your organization type. Provide your institutional or professional affiliation. Confirm whether you are a student. State whether you submitted a conference abstract. State whether you are included as a speaker or panelist in someone else’s proposal. Prepare a focused statement of no more than 150 words. Select only one grant option. Review every response carefully. Submit the form before 23:59 GMT on October 31, 2026. Save evidence that the form was submitted. Monitor your email, including spam and junk folders, for the outcome. Google sign-in is offered as a way to save application progress. Applicants should still prepare the 150-word response in a separate document before entering it into the form. Application Preparation Checklist Before starting the online application, prepare: Your name exactly as used in professional correspondence. A reliable email address. Your country of residence. The name of your employer, university, organization or professional affiliation. Your organization type. Confirmation of your current student status. Details of any conference abstract or session proposal. Confirmation from a session organizer if you may have been included as a speaker. A 150-word funding justification. A realistic estimate of your overall attendance costs. A decision on which one of the three support options to request. A plan for financing travel before the in-person payment date, if requesting travel funding. Practical Tips for Applicants Choose the appropriate grant option Do not automatically select the highest amount. If you can fund your travel but cannot afford conference registration, the registration waiver may be the most suitable request. If you need help with airfare or another travel cost, select either US$500 or US$1,000, subject to the geographical restriction on the US$1,000 option. Address both elements of the main question A response that only explains your professional work is incomplete. You must also explain why you need funding. Similarly, a response that discusses only financial hardship without demonstrating a meaningful connection to the conference may be less persuasive. Emphasize a practical post-conference outcome Explain what you will do with the knowledge and contacts gained. Examples could include: Updating a community conflict-management programme. Sharing lessons with colleagues. Improving a research method. Developing a policy recommendation. Organizing a local training session. Strengthening a cross-border collaboration. Integrating community perspectives into a conservation programme. Do not assume the grant is paid before travel The official payment arrangement states that travel-grant recipients will receive cash in Bangkok on March 3, 2027. Prepare accordingly. Submit early The deadline is fixed at 23:59 GMT on October 31, 2026. Submitting early gives applicants time to address internet, form or email problems. Keep the statement within 150 words Exceeding the maximum length may weaken the application or result in text being cut off. Draft and count the words before pasting the response into the form. Travel-Grant Sponsors The sponsor logos displayed on the official page identify: Fondation Segré. Golden Triangle Asian Elephant Foundation. The conference is organized by the IUCN SSC Human-Wildlife Conflict Coexistence Specialist Group. Other Funding Opportunities Listed by the Conference The official page also refers applicants to two external funding sources: British Ecological Society travel-grant opportunities. Southeast Asian Regional Center for Graduate Study and Research in Agriculture travel grants. These are separate programmes with their own eligibility rules, application procedures and deadlines. Applicants should not assume that the HWCC Conference application automatically places them under consideration for either external opportunity. Conclusion The 2027 HWCC Conference travel-support programme provides an important opportunity for people working on human-wildlife conflict and coexistence to participate in an international gathering in Bangkok. Applicants can request one of three forms of support: free conference registration, US$500 toward travel expenses or US$1,000 toward travel expenses. Priority will be given to residents of countries not classified as high-income, students and people contributing to the conference programme, but the published information does not restrict applications exclusively to these groups. Applicants should carefully consider the payment arrangement before applying. Travel awards are scheduled to be paid in cash at the conference on March 3, 2027, rather than before departure. Successful recipients may therefore need to finance their initial travel and attendance expenses independently. The main application requirement is a concise 150-word explanation of how conference participation will advance the applicant’s work and why financial assistance is needed. Clear, specific and honest responses will be more effective than broad descriptions of conservation challenges. Applications must be submitted in English through the official online form by 23:59 GMT on October 31, 2026 . Applicants are expected to receive the outcome by November 15, 2026.
